16 Blocks (2006).note: Pork belly roasted till the skin shatters, salt and malt vinegar, pickled onions, hot mustard.
steps: Score the skin of the pork belly, pat dry and refrigerate uncovered overnight to dry it out.
Rub the skin with 1 tbsp of the malt vinegar, then the salt.
Roast skin up at 160°C.
Raise to 240°C and roast until puffed and crackling.
Rest, then cut into bite-sized pieces.
Sprinkle with the flaky salt mixed with the last 1 tsp of malt vinegar. Serve with pickled onions and hot mustard.

16 Blocks (2006).note: Six, crisp underneath, with soy, black vinegar and ginger to dip.
ing: 1 tbsp ginger, cut into fine matchsticks
steps: Mix the soy, black vinegar and ginger for dipping.
Fry the dumplings flat side down in oil.
Add the water, cover and steam.
Uncover and fry again until crisp underneath.
Serve straight from the pan with the dip.

16 Blocks (2006).note: Ground chuck and onions worked fine on the griddle, melted American, lettuce, tomato, mayo, toasted hero. Free delivery within 16 blocks.
steps: Fry the onion in the oil on a hot griddle until soft.
Add the mince and chop it up with a spatula as it browns, seasoning well with salt and pepper.
Lay the cheese on top and chop through until melted.
Toast the rolls. Pile in the meat with lettuce, tomato and mayonnaise.

16 Blocks (2006).note: By the slice, two cocoa layers, dark buttercream. Whole cake 16.00, any name on top.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and line two 20cm tins.
Beat the first batch of butter with the caster sugar, add the eggs, then fold in the flour, half the cocoa and the milk.
Bake in the two tins.
Cool the cakes completely.
Beat the remaining butter with the icing sugar and remaining cocoa.
Sandwich and cover the cakes with the buttercream and add candles.

16 Blocks (2006).note: Seattle-style dark roast over ice, condensed milk from the can, pinch of cinnamon.
steps: Brew the coffee strong with the boiling water and let it cool.
Spoon condensed milk into each of 4 glasses.
Fill with ice and pour the coffee over.
Stir well until creamy and dust with cinnamon.

A Bronx Tale (1993).note: Big green olives packed with sharp provolone, crackling crumb, lemon garlic mayonnaise, a pinch of chilli.
steps: Drain the olives and pat dry. Cut the provolone into small sticks and push one into each olive.
Roll in flour, dip in beaten egg, then coat in breadcrumbs.
Stir the lemon zest, juice and garlic into the mayonnaise to make the aioli.
Heat the oil to 180°C and fry in two batches until deep golden, then drain.
Dust with chilli flakes and serve with the garlic mayonnaise.

A Bronx Tale (1993).note: Hot from the oven, brushed with butter, parsley and grated parmesan.
steps: Cut the dough into 12 strips and tie each in a loose knot.
Place on a lined tray, cover and prove in a warm place for 30 minutes.
Bake at 230°C for 12 minutes until golden.
Melt the butter with the garlic over low heat for 2 minutes.
Toss the hot knots with the garlic butter, parsley and parmesan.

A Bronx Tale (1993).note: Slow tomato gravy, pork and beef meatballs, tender ribs, torn basil. Ask for the JoJo portion.
steps: Mix the mince with egg, breadcrumbs, salt and pepper and shape into 12 meatballs.
Brown the meatballs and ribs in olive oil in a heavy pot, turning, then set aside.
Soften the onion, add the garlic, then the tomatoes, water and basil.
Return the meat, cover partly and simmer gently, stirring and adding water if needed. Check the ribs are tender and the meatballs cooked through.
Boil the rigatoni, drain and toss with the sauce. Serve the meat on a platter.

A Bronx Tale (1993).note: Crisp shells piped to order, vanilla ricotta, chocolate chips, pistachio. Every Sunday, one sitting.
steps: Drain the ricotta in a lined sieve in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
Beat with icing sugar and vanilla until smooth, then fold in the chocolate chips.
Pipe into the shells just before serving.
Dip the ends in crushed pistachios. Serve two per person.

A Bronx Tale (1993).note: Short black coffee, anisette or sambuca on the side, lemon peel.
steps: Brew four short espressos into warmed demitasse cups.
Cut four small curls of lemon peel, avoiding the white pith.
Serve the anisette beside each cup for pouring in, with a lemon curl.

A Goofy Movie (1995).note: Panko-crusted white fish, lemon and a pickle and caper tartare.
steps: Cut the fish into fingers and crumb them in flour, egg, then panko.
Stir the mayonnaise with the pickles and capers for the tartare.
Fry in batches in the vegetable oil at 180°C for about 3 minutes until golden, then drain.
Serve with the tartare and lemon wedges.

A Goofy Movie (1995).note: Corn chips, spiced beef, black beans, cheddar, guacamole, sour cream, salsa.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Brown the mince with the onion.
Add the taco spice, black beans and water and simmer.
Spread the corn chips on a large tray, spoon over the mince and cover with cheddar, then bake until melted.
Mash the avocados with lime and salt, dice the tomatoes with coriander, and top the nachos with guacamole, salsa and sour cream.

A Goofy Movie (1995).note: Chargrilled beef sausages in rolls, fried onions, mustard, tomato sauce, buttered corn.
steps: Grill the sausages over hot coals or a barbecue, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Fry the onions in the oil until soft and sweet.
Grill the corn and brush with butter.
Serve the sausages in rolls with the onions, mustard and tomato sauce.

A Goofy Movie (1995).note: Toasted marshmallow and milk chocolate between digestive biscuits.
steps: Toast the marshmallows on skewers over a gas flame or under a hot grill until golden.
Squash each between two biscuits with a square of milk chocolate and leave 30 seconds so the chocolate starts to melt.

A Goofy Movie (1995).note: Cherry syrup blended with crushed ice and a squeeze of lime.
steps: Blend the cordial, ice, water and lime juice until smooth and slushy.
Pour into tall cups and serve with straws before it melts.

After Hours (1985).note: Toasted minis spread thick with chive and black pepper cream cheese, smoked salmon, capers, sesame, poppy seed and garlic. Softer than a paperweight.
steps: Halve the bagels and toast until golden.
Beat the cream cheese with the milk, chives and pepper.
Mix the sesame, poppy seeds, garlic flakes and salt for the bagel seasoning.
Pipe or spread the schmear thickly onto the bagels. Top with salmon, capers and seasoning.

After Hours (1985).note: Vanilla soft serve dipped in dark chocolate that sets to a shell, then crushed peanuts or sprinkles. Better than the truck.
steps: Soften the ice cream on the bench.
Melt the chocolate with the coconut oil, then cool to room temperature.
Pipe the ice cream into the cones with a large star nozzle and freeze.
Dip the tops into the chocolate, then straight into the crushed peanuts or sprinkles.
Freeze until the shell sets.

After Hours (1985).note: Hand-formed chuck, salted right before the flat top, cooked medium under melted cheddar. Raw onion, dill pickles, toasted bun. Hot till close.
steps: Hand-form the mince into four thick patties without overworking it.
Heat a griddle over medium-high heat. Season the patties just before cooking.
Griddle until cooked through and the centre reaches 75°C, topping with cheddar in the last minute.
Toast the buns cut-side down. Assemble with the patties, raw onion and pickles.

After Hours (1985).note: Vanilla butter layers under seven-minute frosting, roughed up with a palette knife to set white and matte. For the sculptors on the block.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C conventional and line a 16cm cake tin.
Beat the butter with half the sugar until pale. Beat in the 2 whole eggs and vanilla, then fold in the flour and milk.
Bake until a skewer comes out clean, then cool completely.
Whisk the egg whites, remaining sugar and water in a heatproof bowl over gently simmering water until thick, glossy and hot throughout.
Remove from the heat and whisk until stiff.
Cover the cake in a thick matte layer, roughly smoothed like plaster. Cut into four.

After Hours (1985).note: Bourbon, lemon, a little sugar and egg white shaken silky, bitters on the foam, a cherry. Tom shakes them hard.
steps: Dissolve the sugar in the hot water and cool.
Shake the bourbon, lemon juice, the cooled syrup and egg white hard without ice, then again with ice.
Strain into 4 ice-filled rocks glasses. Add bitters to each foam and a cherry.

Analyze This (1999).note: Semolina-crusted squid, fried crisp, lemon. As at the Miami wedding. Interrupted.
steps: Slice the squid into rings and soak in the buttermilk for 30 minutes.
Mix the semolina, flour and plenty of salt.
Drain the squid and toss through the flour mix.
Fry in the neutral oil at 190°C in batches for 90 seconds each.
Salt and serve with lemon wedges.
Cut the crusts off the bread and make 4 sandwiches with the mozzarella. Cut each into triangles.
Dip in the eggs beaten with milk, then press into breadcrumbs.
Shallow-fry in 1cm of oil for 2 minutes a side until golden and the cheese melts.

Analyze This (1999).note: Crumbed cutlet, marinara, mozzarella, parmesan, spaghetti. Like his mother made. We won't go there.
steps: Dust the veal in flour, dip in egg and coat in breadcrumbs.
Shallow-fry in the neutral oil, 2 minutes a side, until golden.
Warm about half the passata, top each cutlet with sauce, mozzarella and parmesan and grill until bubbling.
Cook the spaghetti and toss in the rest of the passata, heated.

Analyze This (1999).note: Sweet ricotta, orange zest, chocolate-dipped ends.
steps: Drain the ricotta for 2 hours, then beat with icing sugar and orange zest.
Melt the chocolate and dip the ends of the shells, then let set.
Pipe the filling in just before serving.

Analyze This (1999).note: Gin, red bitter, sweet vermouth, orange.
steps: For each drink, stir equal parts gin, aperitif and vermouth over ice for 20 seconds.
Strain over a big ice cube in a tumbler and add a slice of orange.

Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy (2.note: Baked brie, honey, thyme, walnuts, crackers.
steps: Score the top of the brie, drizzle with honey and scatter over the thyme and walnuts.
Bake at 180°C on a lined tray until molten. Serve with crackers. Baxter would approve.

Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy (2.note: Lime steak, jack cheese, avocado, sour cream.
steps: Mix the steak with the lime juice, garlic and cumin.
Marinate for 1 hour.
Grill the steak hot, 3 minutes a side, then rest and chop.
Bake the fries on a tray at 220°C until crisp.
Cover with Monterey Jack and grill to melt.
Top with the steak, avocado and sour cream.

Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy (2.note: Crisp chicken, corn tortillas, cabbage, salsa, lime cream.
steps: Cut the chicken into strips and coat in the flour mixed with paprika and cumin, then egg, then panko.
Arrange on a lined tray, drizzle with oil and bake at 220°C, turning halfway, until golden and the thickest piece reaches 75°C.
Mix the sour cream with the juice of one lime for the crema, and toss the tomato and onion with the juice of the other lime.
Warm the tortillas as the packet says and fill with chicken, cabbage, salsa and crema. Keep any chilli on the side.
Heat the oven to 180°C conventional and grease a deep 1.5L baking dish with a little of the butter.
Whisk the flour with part of the sugar and the salt, then whisk melted butter, milk, egg and vanilla in another bowl and fold together just until combined.
Spread into the dish. Mix the rest of the sugar with the cornflour and sprinkle over the batter.
Dissolve the golden syrup in the boiling water and pour gently over the back of a spoon without stirring.
Bake on a tray until the sponge is set and a skewer in the sponge comes out clean. The sauce stays underneath.
Rest, then scoop into bowls with the warm butterscotch sauce and vanilla ice cream. All the butterscotch flavour, no whisky.

Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy (2.note: Blackberry and lemon soda, no liquor.
ing: 2 lemons, juiced to give 60ml, plus slices to serve
steps: Simmer the blackberries, sugar and water for 5 minutes, crushing the berries.
Strain and cool completely.
Divide the syrup and lemon juice between ice-filled glasses, top with sparkling water, stir and taste for sugar. Serve with lemon slices. No alcohol.

Annie Hall (1977).note: Sweet meat folded with mayonnaise, lemon, celery and chives on toasted, buttered brioche. By the dozen. Shelled. None behind the refrigerator.
steps: Chop the lobster and fold with mayonnaise, lemon juice, celery and chives.
Spread the brioche slices with the softened butter and cut 16 rounds from them.
Toast the rounds.
Pile the lobster on top.

Annie Hall (1977).note: Flaky pastry around Idahos mashed with slow fried onion, egg washed and baked golden.
steps: Boil the potatoes until tender, then mash.
Fry the onions slowly in the butter.
Mix the onions into the mash with salt and pepper.
Cut each pastry sheet into 4 squares, fill, and pinch closed into rounds.
Brush with egg and bake at 200°C.

Annie Hall (1977).note: Steamed until glossy, piled high on soft white bread with mayonnaise, iceberg and tomato. Yes, we make it. Max winces.
ing: 1 jar yellow mustard, on the side
4 slices of rye bread, on the side
steps: Steam the pastrami until glossy.
Spread the white bread with mayonnaise.
Add lettuce and tomato and pile the pastrami high.
Put rye and mustard on the side for anyone who wants it.

Annie Hall (1977).note: Cream cheese, sour cream and lemon zest on a buttery crumb crust, baked slow in a water bath.
steps: Crush the biscuits, mix with the butter and press into a 22cm tin.
Beat the cream cheese with the sugar, sour cream, eggs and lemon zest.
Pour over the base and bake in a water bath at 150°C.
Cool in the oven.
Chill overnight.

Annie Hall (1977).note: Cucumber, lime, mint and honey blended and strained, poured over ice and topped with seltzer.
steps: Blend one chopped cucumber with the lime juice, honey and mint until smooth, then strain.
Cut the other cucumber into ribbons and fill glasses with ice and ribbons.
Pour some of the mix into each glass and top with sparkling water.
Add a mint sprig.

Back to the Future (1985).note: Hand cut, fried twice. Ready at 88 miles an hour.
ing: 1 L vegetable oil, for deep frying
steps: Cut the potatoes into fries, rinse in cold water and dry thoroughly with a clean tea towel.
Heat the oil in a sturdy deep pan to 140°C and blanch the fries in batches for 5 minutes without browning.
Drain and cool the fries for 15 minutes (this rest is part of the cook time).
Raise the oil to 185°C and fry in batches until crisp, drain, season with salt and serve in paper boats.
Divide the mince into four loose balls and slice the onion very thin.
Heat a griddle until very hot. Put the beef balls on it, top with onion and press firmly into thin patties. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook 3 minutes, flip and cook a further 2 to 3 minutes until the centre reaches 75°C. Lay the cheese on top to melt.
Toast the buns and fill with the patties, pickles and mustard.

Back to the Future (1985).note: Two eggs, bacon and buttered toast, served all day.
steps: Lay the bacon in a cold frying pan and cook over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until crisp. Lift out onto a plate.
Fry the eggs in the bacon fat, spooning the fat over the yolks until the whites are set.
Meanwhile toast the white bread and spread with the butter.
Plate the eggs with the bacon and buttered toast.

Back to the Future (1985).note: Butter cake with vanilla icing, cut thick.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a 20 x 30cm tin. Beat 200g of the butter with the caster sugar until pale.
Beat in the eggs one at a time with the vanilla, then fold in the self-raising flour and 125ml of the milk.
Spread into the tin and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat the remaining 150g butter with the icing sugar and the last 2 tbsp milk until fluffy and spread over the top.
Whisk the cocoa and caster sugar with 100ml hot water until smooth.
Stir in the cold full cream milk and chill for an hour.
Stir again and pour into four tall glasses with a straw each.

Back to the Future (1985).note: Black, nothing added. No Pepsi Free.
steps: Brew the ground coffee with the water in a filter coffee machine or pour-over.
Pour the coffee black into four mugs. No sugar.

Beetlejuice (1988).note: Served lively. Keep your face clear of the bowl.
steps: Poach the prawns in salted simmering water for 2 minutes until just cooked.
Chill in iced water, then drain well.
Mix the mayonnaise, tomato sauce, horseradish, lemon and hot sauce.
Shred half the lettuce into four glasses, pile in the prawns and spoon the sauce over.

Beetlejuice (1988).note: Cheese houses, tomato and cornichon trees. Winter River, to scale. Found in the attic.
steps: Cut the cheddar, gouda and pepper jack into cubes.
Stack the cubes into tiny houses on a long board.
Thread the tomatoes and cornichons onto toothpicks as trees and stand them between the houses, like Adam's model town.

Beetlejuice (1988).note: Garlic and parsley butter, shoestring fries, salad.
steps: Split the lobster tails lengthways. Mash the butter with the garlic, lemon zest and parsley and brush over the flesh.
Cut the potatoes into shoestrings, rinse and dry well.
Fry the potatoes in the vegetable oil in batches at 180°C until crisp, drain and salt.
Grill the lobster flesh side up until just opaque.
Dress the salad leaves in lemon juice and serve with the lobster and fries.

Beetlejuice (1988).note: Vanilla and chocolate sponge, white ganache.
steps: Beat the butter and sugar until pale, add the eggs one at a time and fold in the flour and milk.
Stir the cocoa into half the batter.
Pipe or spoon alternating stripes into a lined loaf tin.
Bake at 170°C until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool the cake in the tin.
Melt the white chocolate with the cream and pour over the cake. Pipe stripes with the melted dark chocolate.

Beetlejuice (1988).note: Banana, lime, sugar syrup and ice. No rum. May cause sudden dancing. Resist.
steps: Dissolve the sugar in the hot water.
Cool the syrup for 10 minutes.
Blend the rum, lime juice, syrup, bananas and ice until smooth and pour into chilled glasses.

Big (1988).note: Charred in butter with crushed red pepper, lime zest and salt.
ing: 2 limes, zested, then cut into wedges
steps: Blanch the baby corn in salted boiling water, then drain well.
Char on a hot griddle with the butter.
Sprinkle with chilli flakes, lime zest and salt.
Serve with lime wedges and eat it like a cob.

Big (1988).note: Salmon roe, crème fraîche and chives on crisp water crackers.
steps: Spread each cracker with crème fraîche.
Top with salmon roe and a few chives.
Assemble just before serving so the crackers stay crisp.

Big (1988).note: Steamed bun, mustard, sauerkraut and onions stewed in tomato.
ing: 3 brown onions, one halved and two sliced
steps: Simmer the franks in water with the halved onion, then griddle until blistered.
Soften the sliced onions in oil, add the tomato paste and vinegar.
Steam the buns.
Fill with franks, mustard, sauerkraut and onions.

Big (1988).note: Brown-butter chocolate chip, iced with piano keys, cut at the table.
steps: Brown the butter and cool.
Beat with the brown sugar and egg, then mix in the flour, bicarb and choc chips.
Press into a pizza tray and bake at 180°C.
Cool completely.
Mix the icing sugar with the water, then pipe piano keys across the cookie.

Big (1988).note: Syrup, cold milk and seltzer, stirred until the foam rises.
steps: Add syrup and milk to each of 4 tall glasses.
Pour in soda water hard from a height, stirring with a long spoon so a white foam head rises.
Serve with a straw straight away.

Big Night (1996).note: Prawns, squid and mussels. No cheese, no spaghetti.
steps: Peel the prawns, scrub and debeard the mussels, dice the onion, chop the garlic and chop the parsley.
Warm the fish stock in a saucepan. Soften the onion and garlic in the olive oil over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add the carnaroli rice and toast for 2 minutes, then pour in the white wine and stir until it is absorbed.
Add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 16 minutes until the rice is nearly tender.
Stir in the prawns, squid rings and mussels, cover and cook for 4 minutes until the mussels open. Throw out any that stay shut.
Take off the heat and stir through the butter, the parsley and a squeeze of lemon. Serve straight away, no cheese.

Big Night (1996).note: Spinach, parmesan and tomato risottos, side by side.
steps: Heat the chicken stock in a saucepan. Soak the saffron in 2 tbsp of hot water. Blitz the baby spinach and basil leaves with a splash of the stock to a smooth paste.
Soften the onion in 40g of the butter for 5 minutes, add the arborio rice and toast for 2 minutes, then add the white wine and stir until absorbed.
Add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 17 minutes until the rice is just tender.

Split the risotto into three pans over low heat. Stir the spinach and basil paste into the first, the parmesan and the last 30g butter into the second, and the passata with the saffron and its water into the third.
Spoon the green, white and red risotto side by side on each plate.

Big Night (1996).note: Ziti, ragù, egg and provolone in a pasta drum. The big night's star.
ing: 3 eggs, boiled and sliced, for the filling
steps: Cook 180g dried ziti in well salted water until just tender, then drain.
Make a dough with the flour and eggs, knead and rest.
Brown the mince with the onion, add the passata and simmer to a ragù.
Roll the dough thin and line an ovenproof bowl greased with the butter.
Toss the cooked ziti with ragù and layer in the bowl with salami, boiled egg and provolone.
Fold the dough over and bake at 180°C for 1 hour.
Rest for 30 minutes, turn out and slice.

Big Night (1996).note: Pork with fennel, garlic and rosemary, for the feast.
steps: Score the skin of the pork belly with a sharp knife. Turn it over and rub the flesh side with the fennel seeds, crushed garlic and chopped rosemary.
Rub the skin with the salt, roll the pork belly up and tie with string every 3cm.
Sit it on a rack and dry uncovered in the fridge overnight.
Roast at 240°C for 30 minutes until the skin starts to blister.
Turn the oven down to 160°C and roast for 2 hours until tender with crisp crackling.
Rest for 15 minutes, cut off the string and carve thick.

Big Night (1996).note: Eggs, olive oil, crusty bread. The silent morning after.
steps: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt.
Heat the olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat, pour in the eggs and stir gently for about 3 minutes until just set underneath and soft on top.
Fold the omelette, slide it onto a plate and cut into four. Serve with the crusty bread torn into pieces.
Mix the pork with the chives, ginger, soy, Shaoxing and sesame oil.
Pleat spoonfuls into the dumpling wrappers.
Fry until the bottoms crisp.
Add the water and steam with the lid on.
Serve with vinegar and chilli oil.
Score the squid and cut into strips.
Toss in the starch with salt, white pepper and five spice.
Heat the vegetable oil to 190°C and fry in batches until crisp.
Wok-toss with fried garlic, red chillies and spring onion.

Big Trouble in Little China (1986).note: Fast hands. It's all in the reflexes.
steps: Toss the beef with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce, the cornflour and 1 tbsp of the oil, and leave for 15 minutes.
Loosen the noodles by hand under warm water and drain well.
Sear the beef in a smoking hot wok with 1 tbsp of the oil for 1 minute, then tip it out.
Fry the onion in the last of the oil, add the noodles and toss over high heat until they catch at the edges.
Add the rest of the soy sauce, the dark soy and sugar, then the beef, bean sprouts and spring onion, and toss for 1 minute. Serve straight away.
Mix the hoisin, honey, soy, five spice, bean curd and garlic and rub over the ribs.
Marinate in the fridge overnight, at least 8 hours.
Roast covered at 160°C.
Uncover, glaze and blast at 220°C until sticky.
Rest briefly before serving.

Big Trouble in Little China (1986).note: Chang Sing or Wing Kong, all order it.
ing: 600g cooked jasmine rice, a day old
steps: Cook 240g jasmine rice ahead (the day before is best), spread it out and chill. Cold rice fries and holds better.
Beat the eggs and scramble them softly in a hot wok with half the oil, then tip them out.
Fry the rice in the rest of the oil over high heat, breaking up the clumps, until it starts to toast.
Add the peas, soy sauce and white pepper, then the egg and spring onion, and finish with the sesame oil.
Trim the gai lan and halve any thick stems.
Blanch in boiling salted water for 1 minute and drain.
Fry the garlic in the oil until golden, then toss the gai lan through with the soy, sugar and water for 1 minute.

Write 12 fortunes on thin paper strips, two of each: It's all in the reflexes. Green eyes mean big trouble. Never lend out your truck. The bag holds six things, don't ask. Pay what you owe before you go underground. Somebody at this table owes you twenty bucks.
Whisk the egg whites with the sugar, then stir in the flour, butter and vanilla.
Spread 8cm circles on a lined tray, a few at a time.
Bake at 180°C.
Working fast, fold each around a paper fortune while hot.

Big Trouble in Little China (1986).note: The flask for the trip below.
steps: Simmer the sugar, water and ginger, then cool and strain.
Shake the plum wine, lemon juice, ginger syrup and egg white hard without ice, then with ice.
Strain into 4 ice-filled glasses and garnish with a pickled plum.

Brewster's Millions (1985).note: Six, poached and chilled, on shredded iceberg with rosy tomato mayonnaise, lemon and paprika.
steps: Poach the prawns in salted water with the lemon and bay leaf, then plunge into iced water and peel.
Mix the mayonnaise, tomato sauce and a squeeze of lemon.
Serve on shredded iceberg in glasses, with sauce and a dusting of paprika.

Brewster's Millions (1985).note: Buckwheat pancakes, crème fraîche, salmon roe, chives.
steps: Warm the blini on a tray at 180°C.
Top each with crème fraîche, then salmon roe and chives.
Serve straight away while warm.

Brewster's Millions (1985).note: An eight ounce filet mignon seared to order and a lobster tail grilled in garlic butter. Béarnaise.
steps: Reduce the vinegar with the tarragon to a few spoonfuls.
Whisk with the yolks over low heat and drizzle in 200g of the warm clarified butter for the béarnaise.
Sear the steaks to medium rare, then rest.
Split the lobster tails and brush with garlic butter made from the remaining butter.
Grill the lobster until cooked through.
Plate the steak with lobster and sauce.

Brewster's Millions (1985).note: Pinked butter shortbread, each iced like a stamp. Six.
steps: Beat the butter with half the icing sugar, then mix in the flours.
Roll to 6mm and cut into rectangles with a pinking cutter.
Bake at 160°C until pale.
Cool completely.
Mix the rest of the icing sugar with a drop of water and pipe a little stamp design on each.

Brewster's Millions (1985).note: A sugar cube soaked in bitters, orange liqueur, chilled brut to the brim and a twist of peel.
steps: Drop a sugar cube into each of 4 flutes and shake bitters onto each.
Add orange liqueur to each glass.
Top slowly with champagne.
Twist a strip of orange peel over each glass and drop it in.

Bugsy (1991).note: Warm buckwheat cakes, crème fraîche, red salmon caviar, snipped chives.
steps: Warm the blini at 180°C for 5 minutes.
Top each with a teaspoon of crème fraîche, salmon roe and chives.
Serve straight away on a tray.

Bugsy (1991).note: Chicken, bacon, avocado, egg, tomato, blue cheese, in lettuce cups.
steps: Poach the chicken for 12 minutes, cool and dice.
Fry the bacon until crisp and crumble. Boil the eggs for 9 minutes and chop.
Dice the avocado and tomatoes.
Fill the lettuce leaves with everything, scatter over the blue cheese and spoon over the vinaigrette.

Bugsy (1991).note: Rib eye pounded thin, seared hot, flamed in brandy, then shallot, Dijon, Worcestershire and cream.
steps: Flatten the steaks and sear hot for 2 minutes a side, then rest.
In the same pan soften the shallots and garlic in the butter, add the brandy and flame.
Stir in the mustard, Worcestershire, stock and cream and reduce.
Return the steaks to coat in the sauce.

Bugsy (1991).note: Crisp meringue, soft middle, whipped cream and crushed raspberries.
steps: Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks, then add the sugar a spoon at a time until glossy.
Fold in the cornflour and vinegar and spread into a round.
Bake at 120°C for 90 minutes, then cool in the oven.
Whip the cream and fold through the raspberries. Pile on top just before serving.

Bugsy (1991).note: A drink for Virginia: gin, fresh lime and soda, shell left in.
steps: Fill four highball glasses with ice.
Add gin and the juice of half a lime to each and drop in the squeezed shell.
Top with soda water.

C.H.U.D. (1984).note: A pull-apart pan, baked this morning with sharp cheese on top.
steps: Fry the onion in some of the butter until golden.
Mix the flour, yeast, salt, sugar, warm milk and the rest of the melted butter. Knead.
Rise in a covered bowl until doubled.
Knead in the onion and most of the cheddar. Shape 12 rolls and pack into a tin.
Rise again.
Top with the remaining cheddar and bake at 200°C.

C.H.U.D. (1984).note: Little rounds of tomato sauce and mozzarella, pepperoni in a crosshatch.
steps: Roll the dough thin and cut 12 rounds.
Spread with sauce and top with mozzarella.
Slice the pepperoni into thin strips and lay them in a crosshatch like a manhole grate.
Bake at 230°C until bubbling.

C.H.U.D. (1984).note: Chuck braised for hours with carrot, celery, onion and potato. Italian bread.
steps: Brown the beef in batches in oil.
Add the onions, carrots, celery and tomato paste and cook.
Add the stock, cover and braise at 160°C.
Add the potatoes and braise for the last hour.
Serve with Italian bread.

C.H.U.D. (1984).note: Boiled-down apple juice in the batter, rolled in cinnamon sugar.
steps: Simmer the apple juice until reduced to a quarter and cool.
Mix with the butter, egg, sugar and flour into a soft dough.
Pat out and cut 12 rings.
Fry in oil at 175°C, turning once.
Toss in caster sugar and cinnamon.

C.H.U.D. (1984).note: Lime cordial and tonic water over a glass full of ice. Glows green under the sign.
steps: Pour cordial into four tall glasses over ice.
Top with tonic water and switch off the lights so it glows under a black light.

Carlito's Way (1993).note: Lacy salt cod fritters with garlic and fresh coriander.
steps: Soak the salt cod in cold water for 24 hours, changing the water three times, then drain and flake.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, water, garlic and coriander into a loose batter and fold in the cod.
Fry wide flat spoonfuls in 180°C oil in batches until golden and lacy.
Drain and salt.

Carlito's Way (1993).note: Green plantain fried twice, smashed flat, spooned with garlic and lime mojo.
steps: Peel the plantains and cut into 3cm chunks.
Fry at 160°C for 4 minutes until soft.
Smash flat with a heavy glass and fry again at 190°C until crisp. Salt well.
Mix the garlic, lime juice and olive oil and spoon over.

Carlito's Way (1993).note: Garlic and oregano pork shoulder, roasted five hours to crackling. Rice with pigeon peas.
steps: Stab the pork all over and rub with garlic, oregano, salt and vinegar. Marinate overnight in the fridge.
Roast skin up at 160°C for 5 hours.
Raise the oven to 230°C for 20 minutes to crackle the skin.
Cook the rice with the drained pigeon peas, stock and onion until tender, and serve alongside the sliced pork.

Carlito's Way (1993).note: Coconut caramel custard, baked slow, turned out cold. One last temptation.
steps: Melt the sugar in a pan until deep amber and pour into a ring tin.
Blend the condensed milk, coconut milk, evaporated milk and eggs and pour over the caramel.
Bake in a water bath at 160°C for 50 minutes until just set.
Chill overnight, run a knife around the edge and turn out onto a plate.

Carlito's Way (1993).note: Dark rum, pineapple, fresh lime and spiced syrup, long over ice, nutmeg grated on top.
steps: Simmer the sugar, water and cinnamon for 3 minutes, then cool.
In a jug, stir the rum, pineapple juice, lime juice, 40ml of the syrup and bitters.
Pour over ice into four tall glasses, grate nutmeg on top and garnish with a lime wheel.

Casino (1995).note: Garlic butter, red pepper, crumbs and crisp bacon.
ing: 4 rashers of bacon, cut into small pieces
steps: Steam the clams in a covered pot until they open, discarding any that stay shut. Remove the top shells.
Mix the butter with the garlic, capsicum, parsley and breadcrumbs.
Top each clam with a spoon of the mix and a piece of bacon.
Grill for 4 minutes until crisp.

Casino (1995).note: On rock salt, spinach and spring onion butter, a dash of anise.
steps: Blitz the spinach, parsley, spring onions, butter, breadcrumbs and liqueur.
Settle the oysters on a tray of rock salt and spoon over the butter.
Grill on high for 3 minutes until bubbling and serve hot with lemon.

Casino (1995).note: Basted in thyme and garlic butter, creamed spinach.
steps: Salt the steaks and leave uncovered on a rack in the fridge overnight.
Sear in a smoking pan for 3 minutes a side, then add the butter, thyme and garlic and baste until 54°C inside.
Rest for 8 minutes while you wilt the spinach, squeeze it dry and simmer with the cream and nutmeg.
Slice the steaks and serve with the creamed spinach.

Casino (1995).note: Buttermilk batter, ten berries in every one.
steps: Whisk the flour, sugar and baking powder.
Mix the eggs, buttermilk and butter and fold into the dry mix until just combined.
Spoon into 12 lined muffin cases and press exactly 10 blueberries into the top of each.
Bake at 190°C for 20 minutes.

Casino (1995).note: Gin, dry vermouth, a green olive. The eye in the sky never blinks.
steps: Freeze four martini glasses for 30 minutes.
For each drink stir gin and vermouth over plenty of ice for 30 seconds and strain into a frozen glass.
Garnish with an olive on a pick.

Chef (2014).note: Cheddar, gruyère and parmesan. Made for Percy, never burnt.
steps: Butter the outside of each slice of bread.
Fill four sandwiches with the cheddar, gruyère and a little parmesan.
Cook slowly in a pan over low heat with a lid on, turning once, until the cheese pours. Cut on the diagonal.

Chef (2014).note: Roast pork, ham, swiss, pickles, mustard. Pressed hot.
steps: Rub the pork with the orange and lime juice, garlic, oregano and salt.
Marinate overnight.
Roast at 160°C for 4 hours until tender, then rest and slice.
Layer the rolls with pork, ham, Swiss, pickles and mustard.
Press and griddle in butter until crisp and the cheese melts.

Chef (2014).note: Garlic, chilli and olive oil. For Molly at midnight.
steps: Thinly slice the garlic and chop the parsley. Bring a big pot of water to the boil and salt it well.
Cook the spaghetti until just shy of al dente and keep 1 cup of the pasta water before draining.
While the pasta cooks, warm the olive oil with the garlic and chilli flakes over low heat until the garlic is pale gold.
Toss the spaghetti through the garlic oil with a splash of pasta water until glossy.
Finish with the parsley, a squeeze of lemon and the parmesan.

Chef (2014).note: Fried yeast dough under icing sugar. The New Orleans stop.
ing: 180ml full cream milk, warmed, for the dough
500ml full cream milk, for the café
steps: Mix the yeast, caster sugar and warm milk and stand for 10 minutes until foamy.
Beat in the egg, melted butter, plain flour and a pinch of salt to a soft dough and knead for 3 minutes.
Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Roll the dough 5mm thick and cut into 6cm squares. Heat the oil to 175°C and fry the squares for 1 minute a side until puffed and golden.
Brew the ground coffee with chicory with 500ml water, heat the milk and mix half and half into four cups.
Drain the beignets and bury them in the icing sugar. Serve with the chicory café.

Chef (2014).note: Molten dark chocolate centre. The Twitter fight cake.
steps: Butter 4 ramekins and melt the chocolate with most of the butter over gentle heat.
Whisk the eggs and yolks with the sugar until thick, combine with the chocolate and fold in the flour.
Bake at 220°C until the edges are set and the centre runs.
Turn out and serve with vanilla ice cream.

Coming to America (1988).note: Thin-cut fries, twice fried and salted straight from the oil.
steps: Cut the potatoes into thin fries and soak in cold water.
Dry well.
Heat the oil to 140°C and fry the potatoes, then rest.
Fry again at 190°C until golden and crisp.
Salt straight away and serve hot.

Coming to America (1988).n: Beef patties from the corner store
Coming to America (1988).note: Spiced beef, curry powder and thyme in flaky golden pastry.
steps: Soften the onion in the oil, then brown the mince with the curry powder, thyme and salt.
Add the stock and simmer until almost dry, then stir in the breadcrumbs and cool.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Brush the pastry sheets with turmeric mixed into the beaten egg and cut two 12cm rounds from each.
Spoon the filling onto half of each round, fold over and crimp with a fork. Brush the tops with the rest of the egg.
Bake on lined trays until golden and flaky, about 25 minutes. Serve hot with hot sauce.

Coming to America (1988).note: Double beef, cheese, pickles, shredded lettuce, onion and house sauce on a three-piece bun. No sesame seeds.
steps: Mix the mayonnaise, relish, mustard, paprika and vinegar for the sauce.
Shape the mince into 8 thin patties.
Smash the patties in a hot pan and add the cheese.
Toast the buns.
Build each with sauce, lettuce, onion, pickles and patties in the three-piece bun.

Coming to America (1988).note: Flaky puff pastry filled with buttery cinnamon apple.
steps: Cook the apples with the butter, sugar and cinnamon.
Cool.
Cut the pastry into quarters, fill, fold into triangles and crimp.
Brush with egg and bake at 200°C.

Coming to America (1988).note: Vanilla ice cream and cold full-cream milk, blended thick.
steps: Chill four tall glasses.
Blend three scoops of ice cream with some of the milk until thick and smooth, one shake at a time.
Pour into a chilled glass and serve with a wide straw.

Die Hard (1988).note: Warm blini, crème fraîche, salmon roe and dill.
steps: Warm the blini on a tray at 180°C.
Top each with crème fraîche and a curl of smoked salmon.
Finish with salmon roe and a dill sprig.
Pass around on a tray straight away.

Die Hard (1988).note: Cashews and almonds, brown sugar butter, cayenne.
steps: Melt the butter with the sugar, rosemary, cayenne and salt.
Toss through the cashews and almonds and spread on a lined tray.
Roast at 170°C, stirring halfway.
Cool so they crisp, then serve warm in a glass bowl.

Die Hard (1988).note: Rare top round, horseradish cream, arugula, pickled onions.
steps: Rub the beef with Dijon, pepper and salt.
Roast at 200°C until 52°C inside.
Rest, then shave thin.
Stir the horseradish into the sour cream.
Split the rolls, spread with horseradish cream and fill with beef, rocket and pickled onions.

Die Hard (1988).note: Vanilla sponge fingers piped with marshmallow cream. A night patrol favourite. Take two for the road.
steps: Beat the butter with half of the sugar, beat in the whole eggs one at a time and the vanilla, then fold in the flour and milk.
Bake in a lined 20 x 30cm tin at 180°C.
Cool and cut into 12 fingers.
Boil the rest of the sugar with the water to 118°C and pour into the egg whites, whisking hard until thick and glossy.
Split the fingers and pipe the cream inside.

Die Hard (1988).note: Bourbon, brown sugar, orange bitters, one big cube.
steps: Dissolve the sugar in the hot water for a syrup.
Stir the bourbon, syrup and bitters with ice in a jug until very cold.
Strain into 4 heavy tumblers over one large ice cube each.
Squeeze orange peel over each, rub the rim and drop it in.

Die Hard with a Vengeance (1995).note: Curried chuck and onion in golden turmeric pastry.
steps: Soften the onion in the oil, then brown the mince with the curry powder, thyme and salt.
Add the stock and simmer until almost dry, then stir in the breadcrumbs and cool.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Brush the pastry sheets with turmeric mixed into the beaten egg and cut two 12cm rounds from each.
Spoon the filling onto half of each round, fold over and crimp with a fork. Brush the tops with the rest of the egg.
Bake on lined trays until golden and flaky, about 25 minutes. Serve hot with hot sauce.

Die Hard with a Vengeance (1995).note: Crisp strips, fried yolk, American, on a toasted buttered kaiser.
steps: Fry the bacon until crisp.
Fry the eggs in the same pan, breaking the yolks, and lay a slice of cheese on each to melt.
Split, butter and toast the rolls. Fill with bacon and egg, season and add tomato sauce.

Die Hard with a Vengeance (1995).note: Buttermilk thighs fried crisp, butter and hot sauce honey.
steps: Soak the chicken in the buttermilk and salt.
Soak in the fridge.
Dredge in the flour mixed with paprika and make the waffle batter.
Fry the chicken in oil at 175°C in batches until at least 74°C inside.
Cook the waffles in a waffle iron. Warm the honey with the hot sauce and drizzle over the chicken on the waffles.

Die Hard with a Vengeance (1995).note: Brown sugar caramel, salted peanuts, milk chocolate, coarse salt.
steps: Line a 20cm square tin. Heat the sugar, butter, cream and golden syrup, stirring, then boil to 118°C.
Stir in the peanuts and pour into the tin.
Cool.
Spread with melted chocolate and sprinkle with flaky salt.
Chill, then cut into squares.

Die Hard with a Vengeance (1995).note: Squeezed lemons, sugar syrup, cold water, over ice.
steps: Dissolve the sugar in the hot water and cool.
Juice about 10 lemons.
Chill the syrup, add the lemon juice and top up with cold water to exactly 4 litres. Serve over ice.

Do the Right Thing (1989).note: Six knots, melted butter, parsley, parmesan.
steps: Cut the dough into 12 strips and tie each into a knot.
Rest the knots on a tray to prove until puffy.
Bake at 230°C until golden.
Melt the butter with the garlic and chopped parsley, toss the hot knots through and shower with parmesan.

Do the Right Thing (1989).note: Ice cold, with mint, lime and chilli salt.
steps: Cut the watermelon into 3cm cubes and the feta into 2cm cubes.
Thread onto the skewers, alternating with small mint leaves.
Mix the salt, chilli flakes and lime zest, squeeze the lime juice over the skewers and sprinkle with the chilli salt. Serve straight from the fridge.
Rest the dough at room temperature for an hour. Season the tomatoes with salt.
Stretch the bases thin and spread with the sauce. Top with the mozzarella and pepperoni.
Bake on a preheated tray at the oven's highest setting until bubbling and charred in spots. Sprinkle with oregano and cut big.

Do the Right Thing (1989).note: Shaved fine, our own syrup, fresh lemon.
steps: Pit the cherries.
Simmer the cherries with the sugar, water and lemon juice, then strain.
Cool and chill the syrup until cold.
Shave or crush the ice into four cups and pour the syrup over just before serving.

Do the Right Thing (1989).note: Ice-cold lager, half and half, lemon wheel.
steps: Juice the lemons and stir the juice with the sugar and cold water until dissolved. Keep a few lemon wheels for the glasses.
Chill 4 tall glasses in the freezer.
Half-fill each glass with ice-cold lager, top with lemonade, then add ice and a lemon wheel. Serve straight away.

Dog Day Afternoon (1975).note: Ridged chips, slow-browned onions in sour cream, cream cheese and chives.
steps: Slice the onions.
Cook the onions in the oil over low heat until deep brown, then cool.
Stir into the sour cream and cream cheese with the chives and salt. Serve with the chips.

Dog Day Afternoon (1975).note: Ham, salami, provolone, iceberg, tomato, oil, vinegar and oregano. Pressed, cut in wedges.
steps: Split the rolls lengthwise.
Layer the ham, salami, provolone, lettuce and tomato.
Dress with the oil, vinegar, oregano, salt and pepper.
Press down firmly, then cut each hero into 6 wedges.

Dog Day Afternoon (1975).note: Thin crust, crushed tomato, oregano, mozzarella and spicy cured sausage.
steps: Rest the dough at room temperature so it relaxes. Season the tomatoes with salt and oregano.
Stretch the bases thin, spread with sauce and top with the mozzarella and pepperoni.
Bake on a preheated tray at the oven's highest setting until bubbling and golden.

Dog Day Afternoon (1975).note: Fresh juice and zest, frozen and scraped fluffy. Paper cups.
steps: Zest 2 lemons and simmer the zest with the sugar and water, then cool.
Juice all the lemons and stir the juice into the syrup.
Freeze in a shallow tray, scraping with a fork every 30 minutes until fluffy.
Serve in paper cups.

Dog Day Afternoon (1975).note: Over two cubes, a fresh squeeze, glass rimmed with chilli salt and zest.
steps: Mix the salt, chilli powder and lime zest on a plate. Run a lime wedge around the rims of 4 chilled glasses and dip in the chilli salt.
Squeeze lime juice into each glass, add ice, then pour in the cold lager slowly.

Donnie Brasco (1997).note: Seared with garlic, chilli flakes, white wine and butter. Bread for the juices.
steps: Butterfly the prawns.
Heat the olive oil until very hot, add the prawns with garlic and chilli and cook.
Add the wine, bubble for a minute, then swirl in the butter and parsley.
Serve in the pan with crusty bread for the juices.

Donnie Brasco (1997).note: Cheese fingers crumbed twice and fried golden, warm tomato sauce to dip.
steps: Cut the mozzarella into 16 fingers and freeze for 20 minutes.
Dip in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, then egg and crumbs again.
Fry in the neutral oil at 180°C for 90 seconds in batches until golden.
Warm the passata with salt and oregano for dipping.

Donnie Brasco (1997).note: Seared hot, glazed with soy, mirin and sake. Steamed rice, bok choy.
steps: Simmer the soy, mirin, sake and sugar for 5 minutes until syrupy.
Cook the rice.
Sear the steaks in a smoking pan for 3 minutes a side, brushing with glaze in the last minute.
Rest for 5 minutes, slice, and blanch the bok choy to serve alongside.

Donnie Brasco (1997).note: Baked slow with lemon zest and vanilla, cooled in the oven.
steps: Drain the ricotta in a sieve for 2 hours.
Beat with sugar, eggs, lemon zest and vanilla until smooth.
Pour into a lined 22cm springform tin and bake at 160°C for 60 minutes.
Turn off the oven and cool inside with the door ajar. Dust with icing sugar to serve.

Donnie Brasco (1997).note: Scotch, sweet vermouth and bitters over one big cube, orange peel, a cherry.
steps: Put four heavy tumblers in the freezer for 15 minutes.
Stir the Scotch, vermouth and bitters with ice in a jug for 30 seconds.
Strain over a large ice cube in each tumbler, twist orange peel over and drop it in, and add a cherry.

Elf (2003).note: Crunchy corn set in maple butter toffee, broken into big chunks. Syrup on every table. Put it on everything.
steps: Pop the corn in the oil in a covered pot.
Boil the maple syrup with the butter to 120°C.
Pour over the popcorn, toss quickly and spread on a lined tray to set. Break into clusters.

Elf (2003).note: Salted pretzel rods in white chocolate, rolled in crushed peppermint.
steps: Melt the white chocolate in a bowl over barely simmering water.
Dip each pretzel rod two-thirds into the chocolate and roll immediately in the crushed candy canes.
Set on baking paper until firm.

Elf (2003).note: Steamed buns, yellow mustard, onions in red sauce, warm sauerkraut.
steps: Slice the onions.
Cook the onions in the butter over medium-low heat until soft.
Add the tomatoes and simmer.
Simmer the franks in water, drain and griddle until browned. Warm the sauerkraut and steam the buns.
Assemble with mustard and the tomato onions.

Elf (2003).note: Vanilla cake, thick cream cheese frosting, rolled in shredded coconut.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C. Beat some of the butter with the sugar, add the egg and vanilla, then fold in the flour and milk.
Divide between 4 large cupcake cases and bake.
Cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese with the remaining butter and icing sugar. Dome over the cakes and roll in the coconut.

Elf (2003).note: Coffee in maple cocoa milk, whipped cream, marshmallows, candy cane.
steps: Whip the cream.
Heat the milk with the chocolate and most of the maple syrup, whisking until smooth and steaming.
Stir in the coffee, or leave it out for the kids.
Pour into 4 mugs and top with cream, marshmallows, a drizzle of maple syrup and crushed candy cane.

Escape from New York (1981).note: Top round soaked in soy and smoked paprika, dried in the oven.
steps: Freeze the beef until firm.
Slice 3mm thick across the grain and mix the marinade from the soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, brown sugar, smoked paprika, chilli flakes and garlic powder.
Marinate the beef in the marinade overnight in the fridge.
Pat dry, lay on racks over trays and dry at 75°C with the oven door slightly open until leathery but still bendy.

Escape from New York (1981).note: Sardines in oil on crackers, lemon, hot sauce and parsley.
steps: Drain the sardines and chop the parsley.
Lay a sardine on each cracker, squeeze over lemon, add a drop of hot sauce and some parsley. Serve on the tin lids.

Escape from New York (1981).note: Smoked sausage, potato, white beans, tomato and cabbage.
steps: Dice the vegetables and slice the sausage. Shred the cabbage.
Brown the sausage in a big pot, then add the onion, carrots and potatoes and cook.
Add the paprika, beans, tomatoes and stock and simmer, adding the cabbage for the last 10 minutes.
Season and serve in mugs.

Escape from New York (1981).note: Buttery baked oats under dark chocolate and flaky salt.
steps: Melt the butter with the golden syrup and sugar, stir in the oats and salt, and press firmly into a lined 20cm square tin.
Bake at 180°C until golden.
Melt the chocolate, spread over the warm slice and sprinkle with flaky salt.
Cool, then chill until firm. Cut into 16 bars.

Escape from New York (1981).note: Corn whiskey, fresh lemon and sugar, shaken, in a jar. Off watch only.
steps: Juice the lemons and stir the sugar into the juice with a little warm water.
Shake the whiskey with the lemon mix and ice, then strain into 4 ice-filled jam jars. Top up with lemonade and lemon for anyone not drinking.

Frequency (2000).note: Beef and kidney bean chilli in baked wonton cups, cheddar melted over.
ing: 1 tsp oil, plus extra to grease
steps: Press the wonton wrappers into a lightly oiled mini muffin tin. Bake at 180°C until crisp.
Brown the mince in oil, add the onion and cook until soft.
Stir in the chilli powder, tomatoes and beans. Simmer until thick.
Spoon into the baked cups, top with cheddar and return to the oven to melt.

Frequency (2000).note: Bicarb soda dip, coarse salt, baked glossy. Honey beer mustard.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and warm water and knead.
Rise in a covered bowl until doubled.
Shape into 8 pretzels.
Boil each briefly in the water with the bicarb, then drain and sprinkle with coarse salt.
Bake at 220°C until deep brown.
Mix the mustard, lager and honey for the dip.

Frequency (2000).note: Thin crust, crushed tomato, mozzarella and crumbled Italian sausage. By the slice. Whole pie $1.69, boxed.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and water and knead. Divide into two balls.
Refrigerate covered to cold-ferment for a day or two.
Bring to room temperature.
Heat a pizza steel at the oven's maximum, about 250 to 275°C.
Remove the sausage from its casings, crumble and pan-fry until cooked.
Stretch the dough thin into two pizzas. Top with tomatoes, mozzarella and sausage.
Bake each on the steel until crisp and cooked, then cut into wedges.

Frequency (2000).note: Tart green apples, cinnamon and sugar, a double crust brushed with egg. Julia bakes it between shifts.
steps: Line a 20cm pie dish with half of the pastry.
Peel, core and thinly slice the apples. Toss with sugar, cinnamon and flour.
Fill the pastry, cover with the rest and crimp. Cut two steam vents, brush with egg and sprinkle with a little sugar.
Bake at 190°C until golden and the apples are tender.
Rest before cutting into four portions.

Frequency (2000).note: Cold lager and fresh lemonade, mint sprig, lemon wheel. Grown-ups only.
steps: Stir the lemon juice, sugar and water until the sugar dissolves.
Chill 4 glasses in the freezer.
Pour lager into each glass and top with lemonade. Add a splash of the lemon mix.
Add a sprig of mint and a lemon wheel.

Friday (1995).note: Never two things that match. Now they do.
steps: Spread peanut butter on four slices of the bread and jam on the other four, then press together.
Butter the outsides of the sandwiches.
Cook in a frying pan over medium heat, pressing down, until golden and the filling is warm, turning once.
Dust with icing sugar, cut into triangles and serve warm.

Friday (1995).n: Porch ham and beef mini burgers
steps: Shape the mince into 12 small patties and season well.
Cook on a hot pan for about 2 minutes a side.
Brown folded ham slices in the pan, top each patty with ham and half a slice of cheddar, and cover for a minute to melt.
Put in the mini burger buns with pickles.
Peel and core the pineapple and cut into 12 long spears.
Heat a grill pan until smoking and char the spears for 2 minutes a side until marked.
Mix the chilli powder, salt, caster sugar and the zest of the lime.
Squeeze the lime over the warm pineapple, sprinkle with the chilli mix and push a skewer into each spear.
Chill for 20 minutes before serving.

Friday (1995).note: Drumsticks, corn, potato salad. Deebo, keep walking.
steps: Toss the drumsticks with salt, pepper and smoked paprika.
Roast at 200°C until starting to colour.
Brush with barbecue sauce and grill or roast, basting twice, until sticky.
Boil the corn for 6 minutes and roll in the butter.
Serve the chicken with the corn and potato salad.

Friday (1995).note: Dipped, crunchy. Big Worm wants his money first.
steps: Melt the chocolate with the coconut oil and let it cool to room temperature.
Scoop the ice cream into the cones.
Freeze the filled cones for 20 minutes.
Dip each top in the chocolate and roll straight away in the crushed cornflakes mixed with sprinkles.
Freeze until serving.

Friday (1995).note: With sugar this time. Big cups, lots of ice.
steps: Blend the strawberries with the sugar and lemon juice, then strain into a big jug.
Add the cherry juice and cold water and stir until the sugar is gone.
Pour over plenty of ice in big plastic cups.

Fried Green Tomatoes (1991).note: Thick slices in buttermilk and cornmeal, fried in bacon drippings. Caper remoulade.
steps: Slice the tomatoes thick, salt them and leave for 10 minutes.
Mix the mayonnaise with chopped capers and lemon juice for the remoulade.
Cook the bacon in a large pan until crisp and the fat has run, and set the bacon aside.
Dip the tomatoes in buttermilk then seasoned cornmeal and fry in the bacon fat until golden, turning once.

Fried Green Tomatoes (1991).note: Hot buttermilk biscuits, sweet butter, bee tree honey and a piece of the comb. Idgie fetches it from the bee tree.
steps: Rub most of the butter into the flour and baking powder.
Fold in the buttermilk, pat out and fold three times, then cut into rounds.
Bake at 220°C until risen and golden.
Serve warm with the remaining butter, honey and a chunk of honeycomb.

Fried Green Tomatoes (1991).note: Pork shoulder roasted slow and pulled, tomato and cider vinegar sauce, slaw, white bread. Ask Sipsey how it's done.
steps: Rub the pork with the paprika, brown sugar, garlic and salt.
Roast covered at 150°C for 5 hours until falling apart.
Simmer the tomato sauce with the vinegar until slightly thick, and pull the pork.
Dress the pork with the sauce. Toss the cabbage with mayonnaise for slaw and serve with white bread. The secret's in the sauce.

Fried Green Tomatoes (1991).note: Toasted pecans in brown sugar and cane syrup custard, flaky crust.
steps: Line a pie tin with the pastry and chill.
Blind-bake with baking weights until pale gold, then remove the weights.
Whisk the eggs, syrup, sugar and melted butter and stir in the pecans.
Pour into the case and bake at 170°C until just set.
Cool before slicing.

Fried Green Tomatoes (1991).note: Brewed strong with ripe peaches, iced, lemon and mint. Out on the porch, where you can hear the trains.
steps: Brew the tea bags in the boiling water with two sliced peaches for 5 minutes.
Remove the bags and stir in the sugar while hot.
Cool completely with the peaches in, then chill and strain.
Pour over ice in tall glasses with lemon, fresh peach slices and mint.

Get Shorty (1995).note: Crisp crumb jacket, creamy centre, nutmeg. Mind the jacket. Ask Ray Bones.
steps: Melt the butter, cook the flour for 1 minute and whisk in the milk until very thick.
Stir in the ham and nutmeg, spread on a tray and chill for 3 hours.
Shape into 20 logs and roll in egg and breadcrumbs.
Fry in the neutral oil at 180°C in batches until golden.
Blitz the mayonnaise, sour cream, a big handful each of parsley and tarragon, half the chives, the anchovies and the lemon juice until smooth and green.
Trim the carrots and radishes, leaving a little green on top. Cut the cucumber into batons and pull the cos into leaves.
Stand the vegetables up in glasses of ice and serve with the green goddess in a bowl.

Get Shorty (1995).note: Sirloin seared hard, red wine and shallot butter, double-fried frites. He knows how this scene goes.
steps: Cut the potatoes into thin frites and fry in the neutral oil at 140°C for 5 minutes, then rest.
Season the steaks and sear hard for 3 minutes a side, then rest.
Sweat the shallots in the pan fat, add the wine and reduce by two thirds, then whisk in the butter.
Fry the frites again in the oil at 185°C until crisp.
Slice the steak and spoon the sauce over.

Get Shorty (1995).note: Vanilla ice cream, hot fudge, caramel corn, salted peanuts. Half a million cheaper than a script.
steps: Pop the popcorn kernels.
Melt the butter with the brown sugar, toss through the popcorn and bake at 150°C for 10 minutes to set.
Melt the chocolate with the cream for hot fudge.
Scoop ice cream into four bowls, pour over the fudge and top with popcorn and peanuts.

Get Shorty (1995).note: Vodka, tomato, lemon, a little heat, a celery stick.
ing: celery salt and pepper, to taste
steps: Put a share of vodka, tomato juice, lemon, Worcestershire, hot sauce, celery salt and pepper in a tin with ice.
Pour back and forth between two tins 5 times.
Strain over fresh ice and add a celery stick. Repeat for each drink.

Ghost Dog: The Way of the Samurai (1999).note: Nuts, pumpkin seeds, soy, honey, sesame.
steps: Toss the nuts and pumpkin seeds with the soy, honey and sesame seeds. Spread on a lined tray.
Roast at 170°C, stirring once.
Cool on the tray so they crisp.

Ghost Dog: The Way of the Samurai (1999).note: Edamame in the pod, salt, sesame oil.
steps: Boil the edamame in salted water and drain well.
Toss with the sea salt and sesame oil and serve warm, with another bowl for the empty pods.

Ghost Dog: The Way of the Samurai (1999).note: Chicken thigh glazed in soy, mirin and sake, short grain rice, pink ginger, spring onion.
steps: Cook the rice and keep warm.
Simmer the soy, mirin, sake and sugar until syrupy.
Sear the chicken skin side down, flip and cook through, then pour in the sauce and turn until glazed.
Slice the chicken over the rice and top with pickled ginger and spring onion.
Toast the coconut in a dry pan until golden.
Blend the coconut cream, cream and sugar until the sugar dissolves, then stir in most of the coconut.
Churn, or freeze in a tub, stirring every hour.
Scoop and finish with the rest of the coconut.

Ghost Dog: The Way of the Samurai (1999).note: Lemons, honey and mint over ice, whisked Japanese tea floated on top.
steps: Juice the lemons. Stir the honey into some warm water, then add the lemon juice and cold water.
Whisk the matcha with hot water (about 80°C) until frothy.
Fill 4 glasses with ice, pour in the lemonade, float the matcha on top and add a lemon wheel and mint. Stir at the table.

Ghostbusters (1984).note: Warm spinach and artichoke dip, green and greedy.
steps: Wilt the spinach in a dry pan, cool, then squeeze very dry and chop with the artichokes.
Mix the spinach and artichokes with the cream cheese, sour cream, most of the mozzarella, the parmesan and the garlic.
Spoon into a small baking dish, top with the rest of the mozzarella and bake at 190°C for 20 minutes until bubbling.
Serve hot with the corn chips for scooping.

Ghostbusters (1984).note: Eggs whipped with Dijon and chives. Zuul lives in the fridge.
steps: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, then cool in iced water and peel.
Halve the eggs and scoop the yolks into a bowl.
Whip the yolks with the mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, a pinch of salt and a drop of green food colouring until smooth.
Pipe back into the whites and scatter the chives on top.

Ghostbusters (1984).note: Meatballs in red sauce on a long roll, long enough for the whole crew.
steps: Mix the pork and beef mince with the egg, parmesan, breadcrumbs, garlic, salt and pepper and roll into 16 meatballs.
Bake the meatballs on a lined tray at 200°C for 15 minutes.
Simmer the passata with the oregano, add the meatballs and simmer for 15 minutes.
Split the long rolls, pack in the meatballs and sauce and lay the provolone on top.
Grill for 2 to 3 minutes until the cheese has melted.

Ghostbusters (1984).note: Lap cheong rice and pork dumplings, out of the boxes.
steps: Cook the jasmine rice the day before, spread it on a tray and chill overnight.
Slice the lap cheong and spring onions and beat the eggs.
Heat a wok until smoking with half the oil, scramble the eggs, then add the lap cheong, rice and 2 tbsp soy sauce and toss for 4 minutes until hot. Stir through the spring onions.
Fry the frozen pork dumplings in the rest of the oil in a frying pan for 2 minutes until the bases brown, add the water, cover and steam for 6 minutes.
Serve out of takeaway boxes with the rest of the soy sauce on the side.

Ghostbusters (1984).note: Marshmallows toasted golden on skewers, Camp Waconda style.
steps: Melt the dark chocolate in a bowl over simmering water and crush the digestive biscuits in a bag with a rolling pin.
Push 2 marshmallows onto each bamboo skewer.
Toast over a gas flame or under a hot grill, turning often, until the outside blisters.
Dip in the melted chocolate, then in the crushed biscuits, and eat while warm.

Ghostbusters (1984).note: Marshmallow and chocolate on biscuits. Toast till he melts.
steps: Lay 8 digestive biscuits on a tray and put a square of milk chocolate on each.
Toast the marshmallows over a flame until golden and melting, or sit one on each chocolate square and put the tray under a hot grill for 30 seconds.
Press the remaining biscuits on top and eat straight away.

Ghostbusters (1984).note: Lime slushie, very green. Not EPA approved.
steps: Blitz the ice with the lime cordial and lemonade until slushy.
Add a drop of green food colouring and blitz again.
Pour into 4 glasses and add a slice of lime to each.

Ghostbusters II (1989).note: Roast beets, feta, yoghurt, garlic, lemon and dill, with warm flatbread.
steps: Wrap the beetroots in foil.
Roast at 200°C until tender, then cool a little and peel.
Blitz the beetroot with the feta, yoghurt, garlic, lemon juice and a little dill until bright pink and smooth. Warm the flatbreads, cut into wedges and serve for scooping.

Ghostbusters II (1989).note: Honey butter. Play them something upbeat.
steps: Beat the butter with the honey and salt.
Toast the crumpets until the holes are crisp.
Spread with the honey butter while hot so it runs into the holes, then cut into quarters.

Ghostbusters II (1989).note: Slow paprika beef, onions, caraway and tomato. Egg noodles, sour cream.
steps: Brown the beef in batches in a hot pan with oil.
Cook the onions slowly in the same pot until soft.
Stir in the sweet paprika, hot paprika and caraway, then add the tomatoes, stock and beef.
Cover and braise at 160°C until the beef is very tender.
Boil the noodles and serve the goulash over them with the sour cream.

Ghostbusters II (1989).note: Raspberries inside. It wobbles to music. Keep cheering, kids.
steps: Soak the gelatine leaves in cold water.
Warm part of the lemonade, squeeze the gelatine and stir in until melted, then add the rest of the lemonade.
Pour into a jelly mould with the raspberries.
Chill in the fridge until set.
Dip the mould in hot water, turn out and put on something upbeat.
Put a scoop of raspberry sorbet in each of four tall glasses.
Pour chilled pink lemonade slowly over the top so it fizzes up pink. Serve with a spoon and a straw.

Goodfellas (1990).note: Sliced the way Paulie does it inside.
steps: Slice the garlic paper thin on a mandoline.
Cook the garlic in the olive oil over low heat until soft and barely golden.
Grill the bread, rub with the cut side of the tomatoes and season with salt.
Spoon over the garlic and its oil and finish with torn basil.

Goodfellas (1990).note: With pepperoncini and bread, laid out like the cell.
steps: Cut the provolone into thick batons.
Arrange the salami, prosciutto and provolone on a board.
Put the pepperoncini and marinated mushrooms in small bowls beside the board.
Tear the Italian bread by hand and set it next to the board.

Goodfellas (1990).note: Veal, beef and pork. Go easy on the onions.
steps: Soak the bread in the milk, then mix with the minces, egg, pecorino, parsley and 1 crushed garlic clove.
Roll into 16 balls and brown in olive oil.
In the same pot gently cook the remaining garlic sliced razor thin and the onion, add the tomatoes and the meatballs, and simmer.
Cook the spaghetti and serve with the sauce and meatballs.

Goodfellas (1990).note: Rump in butter and garlic, rare or medium. Funny how?
steps: Take the rump steaks out of the fridge 30 minutes early and season well with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy pan until smoking.
Cook the steaks two at a time, 2 to 3 minutes each side for rare or 4 minutes for medium.
In the last minute add the butter and smashed garlic and spoon them over the steaks.
Rest the steaks for 5 minutes before serving.

Goodfellas (1990).note: Short glasses of Chianti, like inside.
steps: Open the bottles of Chianti and Montepulciano red wine an hour before dinner and leave them to breathe.
Pour the wine into short tumblers at the table.

Home Alone (1990).note: Plain cheese, cut in triangles. Buzz ate the last plain cheese. Not this time.
steps: Simmer the tomatoes with the garlic and oregano for 10 minutes and cool slightly.
Stretch the dough thin on a tray and spread with the sauce, then cover with mozzarella.
Bake on a hot tray at the oven's highest heat until bubbling.
Cut into triangles.

Home Alone (1990).note: Macaroni, cheddar sauce, crumb on top. Heated up all by himself.
steps: Cook the macaroni in boiling salted water 2 minutes short of the packet time and drain.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the milk until thick.
Stir in the cheddar and mustard, then fold through the macaroni.
Tip into a baking dish and top with breadcrumbs.
Bake at 200°C until golden and bubbling.

Home Alone (1990).note: Two ice creams, hot fudge, the lot. Built in front of Angels with Filthy Souls.
steps: Stand the vanilla and chocolate ice cream on the bench for 10 minutes to soften.
Melt the dark chocolate with 150ml of the thickened cream over low heat, stirring, for hot fudge.
Whip the rest of the cream to soft peaks.
Chop the roasted peanuts and put them, the mini marshmallows, sprinkles and maraschino cherries in small bowls.
Set everything out with big bowls and let everyone build their own sundae.

Home Alone (1990).note: Ice cold milk, chocolate malt and a scoop of ice cream, blended. Mind the plane tickets.
steps: Blend the milk, six scoops of ice cream, malted milk powder and some of the chocolate syrup for 30 seconds until thick.
Drizzle chocolate syrup inside tall glasses, pour in the shake and top with whipped cream and a cherry.

Home Alone (1990).note: Big glass, lots of ice. Easy on the refills.
steps: Chill the cola in the fridge overnight, or at least 4 hours.
Slice the lemon and fill four tall glasses with ice, dropping a lemon slice into each.
Pour the cola and go easy on the refills.

Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992).note: Nuts roasted with rosemary and brown sugar, chocolate almonds and pretzels.
steps: Melt the butter with the brown sugar and rosemary, then toss through the nuts.
Spread on a tray and roast at 170°C, stirring once.
Cool completely, then mix with the chocolate almonds and pretzels.

Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992).note: Chicken, crisp bacon, iceberg, tomato and mayonnaise on toasted white.
steps: Poach the chicken breasts in simmering water until cooked through, then slice.
Grill the bacon until crisp.
Toast the bread and spread with mayonnaise. Slice the tomatoes and shred the lettuce.
Build 4 triple-deckers with chicken, bacon, lettuce and tomato. Cut into quarters and pin each with a toothpick.

Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992).note: Butter-poached tail meat and elbows in Gruyère and cheddar sauce, baked under golden crumbs. Served until 2 a.m.
steps: Cook 180g dried macaroni in well salted water until just tender, then drain.
Remove the lobster meat from the shells. Boil the macaroni and drain well.
Gently poach the lobster meat in some of the butter, then chop.
Melt more butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the warm milk and simmer. Stir in the Gruyère and cheddar.
Fold through the macaroni and lobster and tip into a baking dish.
Top with the panko mixed with melted butter and bake at 200°C until golden.

Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992).note: Rolled up: vanilla ice cream, hot fudge, whipped cream, nuts, sprinkles, cherry.
steps: Melt the chocolate with some of the cream for the hot fudge.
Whip the remaining cream.
Pile the ice cream into four tall glasses, pour over the fudge, then add cream, nuts, sprinkles and a cherry on each.

Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992).note: Mulled with cinnamon, cloves and orange, warm in a mug.
steps: Peel strips of orange peel.
Warm the apple juice with some of the cinnamon sticks, the cloves, peel and sugar over low heat without boiling.
Strain into 4 mugs and serve steaming with a fresh cinnamon stick in each.

Hook (1991).note: Melon, kiwi, pineapple and blueberries in rainbow rows, lime and honey drizzle. Real fruit, for a grown-up who can't imagine it yet.
steps: Cut the watermelon, rockmelon, kiwifruit and pineapple into chunks.
Arrange in rainbow rows with the blueberries.
Drizzle with lime juice mixed with honey.

Hook (1991).note: Beetroot hummus, pea and mint, and cumin carrot, with warm pita chips. Made for flicking across the table. Bangarang, Rufio!
steps: Blitz 1 drained 400g tin chickpeas with 2 tbsp tahini, lemon, garlic and 3 tbsp oil, then split in two.
Blend one half with 1 cooked beetroot.
Blend 200g frozen peas, cooked, with mint, 50g feta and lemon.
Boil 3 carrots until soft and blend with 1 tsp cumin, honey and oil.
Cut 3 pitas into wedges, brush with oil and bake at 180°C for 8 minutes.

Hook (1991).note: Buttered white bread covered in rainbow sprinkles, cut into triangles. For Tink. She once drank poison for Peter.
steps: Spread the bread with butter right to the edges.
Press face down into the rainbow sprinkles and dust with sparkling sugar.
Trim the crusts and cut into triangles.

Hook (1991).n: Lost Boys roast chicken, potatoes and corn
Hook (1991).note: Spatchcock chicken with garlic, lemon and smoked paprika, roast potatoes, grilled corn. “I want steak, I want eggs, I want a cup of coffee.” Peter, before he imagines it.
steps: Spatchcock the chicken and rub with crushed garlic, lemon zest and paprika. Chop the potatoes.
Roast at 220°C with the potatoes in the tray.
Grill the corn cobs, turning until charred.
Pile it all in the middle and eat with your hands. Bangarang.

Hook (1991).note: Chuck braised with smoked paprika, tomato and molasses, with cheesy damper. From the galley of the Jolly Roger, for Hook's crew.
steps: Brown 1.2kg diced beef chuck in batches.
Cook 2 onions and 2 carrots 5 minutes, add 2 tsp smoked paprika, 2 tbsp tomato paste, 1 tbsp molasses, 400g tinned tomatoes and 600ml beef stock.
Cover and braise at 160°C for 3 hours.
Rub 50g butter into 300g self-raising flour, add 80g cheddar and 200ml milk, shape into 8 rounds and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes.

Hook (1991).note: Pandan sponge with pandan buttercream and a chocolate clock face piped on top. Hook turned the crocodile into a quiet clock.
steps: Whisk the eggs with the sugar until thick, then fold in the flour, 60g melted butter and half the pandan.
Bake in a lined tin at 175°C.
Cool the cake.
Beat the remaining butter with the icing sugar and rest of the pandan, then cover the cake.
Pipe a clock face with melted dark chocolate.

Hook (1991).note: Cold lemonade, fresh lime juice and a pinch of sparkling sugar. Peter ran out of fairy dust. Tink has plenty.
steps: Pour the cold lemonade into a jug with the lime juice.
Stir in the sparkling sugar and pour into four glasses straight away.

Inside Man (2006).note: Sixteen thin rounds, tomato, mozzarella, pepperoni.
steps: Roll the dough thin and cut 16 rounds with a glass.
Top each with a spoon of sauce, a pinch of mozzarella and a slice of pepperoni.
Bake at 230°C until golden underneath.

Inside Man (2006).note: Potato, onion cooked slow in butter, white pepper, flaky dough, baked golden. Hot mustard.
ing: salt and white pepper, to taste
steps: Boil the potatoes until tender, drain and mash.
Cook the onion in the butter over low heat until soft and mix into the mash with salt and white pepper.
Spread along the pastry, roll into logs, cut into 8 and brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 200°C until golden. Serve with the mustard.

Inside Man (2006).note: Seared hard, sliced thin, jammy onions, arugula, horseradish cream, toasted bread.
steps: Slice the onions.
Cook the onions in the butter over low heat until jammy.
Sear the steaks hard on both sides, rest, then slice thin.
Split and toast the ciabatta, spread with horseradish cream and pile with steak, onions and rocket.

Inside Man (2006).note: Three almond layers, green, white and red, apricot jam between, dark chocolate on top.
steps: Beat the butter with the sugar, then beat in the eggs, almond meal and flour. Divide into 3, tint one green and one red with the food colouring.
Spread each into a lined 20x30cm tin.
Bake each layer at 180°C until just set, in batches, then cool.
Stack the layers with jam between.
Press under a tray in the fridge overnight.
Spread with melted dark chocolate, set, and cut into small squares.

Inside Man (2006).note: A double shot over ice and tonic water, an orange slice. Stir before you sip.
steps: Brew 4 double espressos and let them cool for a few minutes.
Fill 4 tall glasses with ice and an orange slice each, add chilled tonic, then pour an espresso slowly over the back of a spoon so it floats on top. Stir at the table.

Julie & Julia (2009).note: Toasted ciabatta rubbed with garlic, ripe tomato, basil, olive oil.
steps: Dice the tomatoes, salt them and leave 10 minutes.
Toast the ciabatta slices and rub with the cut garlic.
Mix the tomatoes with basil and oil and pile on just before serving.

Julie & Julia (2009).note: Warm Gruyère choux puffs, a grating of nutmeg. Practice for the cooking school.
steps: Boil the water with the butter, beat in the flour and cook for a minute.
Cool slightly, beat in the eggs one at a time, then the gruyère and nutmeg.
Pipe small rounds onto lined trays.
Bake at 200°C until puffed and golden. Bon appetit.

Julie & Julia (2009).note: Beef braised in red wine, bacon, carrots, onions, mushrooms. Attempt number two. Nobody fell asleep.
ing: 2 thyme sprigs of and 2 bay leaves
steps: Dry the beef and brown it in batches with the lardons.
Soften the carrots, onion and garlic in the same pot.
Return the meat, add the wine, stock, thyme and bay leaves and bring to a simmer.
Braise covered at 160°C for 3 hours until the beef is tender.
Glaze the pearl onions and mushrooms in the butter and stir through at the end.

Julie & Julia (2009).note: Chocolate almond cake, soft middle, dark chocolate glaze. The Queen of Sheba. A cake from the book.
steps: Melt most of the chocolate with most of the butter and cool a little.
Separate the eggs and beat the yolks with the sugar, add the chocolate, then fold in the almond meal and flour.
Whip the whites and fold in.
Bake in a lined tin at 180°C, then cool.
Melt the remaining chocolate with the remaining butter and glaze the cake.

Julie & Julia (2009).note: Dry white Burgundy poured over crème de cassis, a blackberry.
steps: Chill the bottle for 2 hours.
Pour the cassis into wine glasses, top slowly with the cold Burgundy or chardonnay so it blends from the bottom, and drop a blackberry in each. Serve before the bourguignon.

Jurassic Park (1993).note: Smoked chicken, avocado, cream cheese, chives.
steps: Mix the cream cheese with the chives and the lemon zest.
Mash the avocado with a squeeze of the lemon and the salt.
Spread all the bread with the cream cheese. Top four slices with avocado and chicken and close with the rest.
Press lightly, cut off the crusts and cut each into three fingers.
Stack in a tin, cover and chill until serving.
Cut the tortillas into curved claw shapes.
Brush with oil and sprinkle with half the salt and the smoked paprika.
Bake at 200°C on lined trays until crisp.
Mash the avocados with the lime juice and remaining salt for the guacamole. Serve with the crisps.

Jurassic Park (1993).note: Minted pea puree, roast baby potatoes.
steps: Brush the lamb racks with Dijon, then press on the parsley and breadcrumbs.
Toss the potatoes in oil and salt and put on a tray in a 220°C oven.
Roast the lamb alongside the potatoes until 55°C inside, about 20 minutes.
Rest the lamb 10 minutes while you boil the peas with the mint, drain and blitz with the butter. Slice the lamb and plate neatly.

Jurassic Park (1993).note: Vanilla bean, hot fudge, honeycomb candy.
steps: Melt the chocolate with the cream over low heat for hot fudge, stirring until smooth.
Leave the ice cream out for 10 minutes so it softens a little too much.
Scoop three each into chilled coupes, pour over the fudge and scatter with crushed honeycomb.

ing: 12 mint leaves, plus extra to serve
steps: Brew the tea bags in boiling water for 5 minutes, remove and stir in the honey.
Cool, then chill for 2 hours.
Muddle the mint with the juice of 2 limes in a jug, add the tea and stir.
Fill tall clear glasses with ice, pour in the tea and garnish with lime wheels and mint.

King of New York (1990).note: Pork and chive, fried crisp, black vinegar, soy and chilli oil.
steps: Mix the black vinegar, soy sauce and chilli oil for dipping.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and pan-fry the dumplings until the bottoms crisp.
Add the water, cover immediately and steam until cooked through (or the packet time), then remove the lid and let the water evaporate.
Serve with the dipping sauce.

King of New York (1990).note: Iced jumbos on shredded iceberg, sharp horseradish red sauce.
steps: Poach the prawns in simmering salted water.
Plunge into iced water, peel and chill.
Mix the tomato sauce, horseradish, juice of half the lemon and a dash of Worcestershire.
Fill 4 glasses with shredded iceberg, hang the prawns over the rims and spoon the sauce in the middle.

King of New York (1990).note: Seared and rested, brandy cream pepper sauce, pommes frites.
ing: 800g rib eye steak, in four pieces
