steps: Cut the potatoes into thin frites, rinse and dry thoroughly.
Fry the frites in oil at 140°C, then drain and cool.
Fry again at 185°C until crisp. Season with salt.
Pat the steaks dry and season. Sear in a heavy pan on both sides, then rest.
Add the cracked black peppercorns to the pan, then carefully add the brandy away from the flame. Add the stock and reduce.
Add the cream and simmer. Serve the steaks with the sauce and frites.

King of New York (1990).note: Cream cheese, sour cream and lemon on a buttered crumb crust.
steps: Line a 16cm springform tin and wrap the outside in two layers of foil. Crush the biscuits, mix with melted butter and press into the base.
Beat the cream cheese with the sugar, then beat in the sour cream, eggs and lemon zest. Pour into the tin.
Set the tin in a roasting pan with hot water halfway up its sides. Bake at 150°C until the edges are set and the centre gently wobbles.
Turn off the oven, leave the door ajar and cool inside.
Refrigerate overnight, then cut into generous slices.

King of New York (1990).note: Sugar cube, bitters and cognac under chilled brut.
steps: Put a sugar cube in each flute and shake bitters onto each. Add cognac, top slowly with chilled champagne and twist a strip of lemon peel over each glass.

Kung Fu Panda (2008).note: Shifu makes Po fight for the last one.
steps: Mix the pork with the wombok, ginger and spring onions and season.
Fold spoonfuls into the wrappers, sealing the edges with water.
Steam in batches over simmering water until cooked through.
Mix the soy, black vinegar and chilli oil for dipping.

Kung Fu Panda (2008).note: From the tree where Oogway sits.
steps: Halve and stone the peaches.
Grill the peaches cut side down until caramelised.
Whip the ricotta with a spoon of honey and the cinnamon, then serve with the peaches, more honey and the almonds.

Kung Fu Panda (2008).n: Mr Ping's red bean steamed buns
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, caster sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl, then add the warm milk and oil and bring together into a dough.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and prove in a warm spot for 1 hour.
Divide into 12, flatten each piece, fill with a tablespoon of red bean paste and pinch closed. Sit each bun on a square of baking paper in a bamboo steamer.
Cover and prove the buns for another 20 minutes.
Steam over boiling water for 12 minutes and serve hot, stacked in the steamer.
Put the frames in a pot with the ginger, garlic and spring onions and cover with the water.
Simmer gently for 3 hours, skimming now and then, then strain. Poach the chicken thighs in the stock for the last 15 minutes.
Season the stock with soy and white pepper and shred the chicken.
Cook the noodles and bok choy briefly, then pour the hot stock over them with the chicken. The secret is there isn't one.

Kung Fu Panda (2008).n: Valley of Peace kung pao chicken
Kung Fu Panda (2008).note: The busy village below the Jade Palace.
steps: Rinse the jasmine rice, then simmer covered in 450ml water on low for 15 minutes and rest off the heat.

Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce and the 1 tbsp cornflour for the chicken. Mix the remaining 3 tbsp soy, the black vinegar, sugar, the cornflour for the sauce and 60ml water for the sauce.
Slice the garlic, grate the ginger and cut the spring onions into 3cm lengths.
Heat the oil in a wok until very hot, stir-fry the dried chillies and Sichuan peppercorns for 20 seconds, then add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and spring onion, then the sauce, and toss until glossy. Stir in the peanuts and serve with the rice.
Beat the butter and sugar, then mix in the almond meal and flour.
Roll into 16 balls, press an almond on each and brush with egg.
Bake at 170°C until golden.

ing: 3 ripe peaches, 2 for the puree and 1 for slices
steps: Steep the tea bags in the water for 3 minutes, remove and chill.
Blend two peeled peaches with the honey and lemon juice until smooth.
Stir the puree into the cold tea and pour over ice with thin peach slices.

Lady and the Tramp (1955).note: Italian loaf, parsley butter, parmesan, baked crisp at the edges.
steps: Mash the butter with the garlic, parsley and parmesan.
Split the loaf and spread thickly.
Bake at 200°C until crisp at the edges, then cut into thick slices and serve in the alley behind the restaurant.

Lady and the Tramp (1955).note: Salami, provolone, olives, artichoke hearts, roasted red peppers, torn bread.
ing: 2 red capsicums, roasted and cut into strips
steps: Fold the salami and provolone onto a board.
Add the olives, artichoke hearts and strips of roasted capsicum.
Tear the bread and set it beside the board. Serve by candlelight.

Lady and the Tramp (1955).note: Beef and pork meatballs, slow tomato and basil. Save the last meatball for your sweetheart. For two, on one plate, .55
ing: 60g parmesan, grated, plus extra to serve
steps: Mix both minces with the parmesan, parsley and egg and roll into balls.
Brown the meatballs in the oil in batches.
Add the tomatoes and basil and simmer gently until the sauce is thick and the balls are cooked through.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente and pile on one big plate with the sauce. Leave the last meatball for your date.
Tip the ricotta into a sieve over a bowl.
Drain overnight in the fridge.
Beat the ricotta with the icing sugar and orange zest, then fold in the chocolate chips.
Spoon into a piping bag, fill the shells just before serving, and dip each end in pistachios.

Lady and the Tramp (1955).note: Rosemary syrup, lemon, soda water. Red as the checked cloth.
ing: 2 rosemary sprigs, plus small sprigs to serve
steps: Simmer the sugar, water and rosemary for 3 minutes.
Cool and strain.
Mix the blood orange juice, syrup and lemon juice in a jug.
Fill glasses with ice, pour in the juice to halfway, top with soda water and garnish with an orange slice and a rosemary sprig.

Léon: The Professional (1994).note: Crusty bread spread thick with sweet butter, thin boiled ham and little sour pickles, cut in twelve.
steps: Warm the baguette at 200°C and cool slightly.
Split lengthways and spread both sides generously with butter. Lay the ham inside, add cornichons and pepper.
Close, press firmly and cut into 12 pieces. Serve with Dijon on the side.

Léon: The Professional (1994).note: Warmed in oil with orange peel, thyme and garlic, with cornichons and pickled onions.
steps: Peel a few strips of orange peel.
Warm the olives gently in the oil with the peel, thyme and garlic.
Tip into a bowl and serve with cornichons and pickled onions in little dishes.

Léon: The Professional (1994).note: San Marzano tomatoes crushed by hand, garlic cooked slow, basil and a knob of butter. Parmigiano on the side. Ask for Tony.
steps: Slice the garlic and cook gently in the oil.
Crush the tomatoes by hand, add with a good pinch of salt and simmer.
Cook the spaghetti, toss through the sauce with basil and butter, and finish with parmesan.

Léon: The Professional (1994).note: Chocolate mousse and cookie soil in a clay pot, a mint sprig growing out the top.
steps: Melt the chocolate and cool slightly, then whisk in the yolks.
Whip the cream and whites separately, then fold both through the chocolate.
Layer in four small cups with the crushed biscuits as soil.
Chill until set, then plant a mint sprig in each.

Léon: The Professional (1994).note: Milk, ice cream, malt and honey, frosted glass.
ing: 4 tbsp malted milk powder, for the shake
2 tbsp malted milk powder, for dusting
steps: Chill 4 tall glasses in the freezer.
Blend the milk, ice cream, the 4 tbsp malted milk powder and honey until thick and smooth.
Pour into the frosted glasses and dust with the 2 tbsp malted milk powder for dusting.

Manhattan (1979).note: Toasted bagels, cream cheese, sliced Nova, capers, red onion cut thin and fresh dill. Wrapped to go for the bench by the bridge.
steps: Whip the cream cheese with the milk until light.
Split and toast the bagels.
Spread thickly, then layer with salmon, capers, onion and dill.
Cut in half and serve on a board.

Manhattan (1979).note: Little rounds of French bread, toasted. Ricotta with lemon peel and honey, or mushrooms, garlic and thyme under Parmesan.
ing: 2 tbsp olive oil, plus extra to brush
steps: Slice the baguette into 20 rounds, brush with oil and toast at 200°C.
Whip the ricotta with the lemon zest.
Fry the mushrooms with thyme and garlic until golden.
Top 10 toasts with ricotta and a drizzle of honey.
Pile the mushrooms on the other 10 with parmesan.

Manhattan (1979).note: Diced dark meat stir-fried hot with dried red peppers, soy, rice wine and black vinegar. Roasted peanuts, spring onions and rice.
steps: Marinate the chicken in some of the soy and the cornflour.
Cook the rice.
Fry the chillies and Sichuan pepper in hot oil, then add the chicken and stir-fry.
Add the vinegar, remaining soy, sugar and Shaoxing and toss until glossy.
Add the peanuts and spring onions and serve with rice.

Manhattan (1979).note: Lemon and vanilla on a buttery crumb crust. Baked slow, chilled overnight. Worth living for, the regulars say.
steps: Crush the biscuits, mix with the butter and press into a 20cm tin. Bake at 160°C.
Beat the cream cheese with sugar, eggs, sour cream, vanilla and lemon zest.
Pour in and bake at 150°C.
Cool in the oven with the door ajar.
Chill overnight.

Manhattan (1979).note: Rye, sweet vermouth and bitters, stirred cold, with a cherry. The pitcher for your table, 17.00.
steps: Chill four coupes.
Stir the rye, vermouth and bitters over plenty of ice, one or two at a time.
Strain into the coupes and drop in a cherry.

Mean Streets (1973).note: Charred onion and red pepper, hot mustard.
steps: Grill the sausages over high heat, turning, until blistered and cooked through.
Toss the capsicum and onion in oil and grill until charred at the edges.
Slice the sausages thick and thread onto toothpicks with the capsicum and onion.
Serve with the hot mustard.

Mean Streets (1973).note: Squid rings, crisp semolina coat, lemon.
steps: Slice the squid into rings and soak in the buttermilk for 30 minutes.
Mix the semolina, flour and plenty of salt.
Drain the squid and toss in the flour mix.
Fry in 190°C oil in batches for 90 seconds each until pale gold.
Salt and serve with lemon wedges.

Mean Streets (1973).note: Garlic, hot chilli, tomato, parsley, pecorino.
steps: Gently fry the garlic and chilli in the olive oil.
Add the tomatoes, season well and simmer.
Cook the penne until al dente and toss through the sauce with a splash of pasta water and parsley.
Finish with the pecorino.

Mean Streets (1973).note: Fried dough, shaken hot in icing sugar.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and warm water into a sticky batter.
Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Drop teaspoons into 175°C oil and fry in batches for 3 minutes until puffed and golden.
Drain, tip into a paper bag with icing sugar, shake and eat hot.

Mean Streets (1973).note: Chilled red over sliced white peaches. Jug 3.50.
ing: 750ml light Italian red, such as Lambrusco secco or young Chianti
steps: Halve, stone and thinly slice the peaches into a large jug. Sprinkle with the sugar and leave for 10 minutes.
Pour over the light Italian red and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Serve in tumblers with a spoonful of peach in each. Eat the peaches last.

Mickey Blue Eyes (1999).note: Cucumber, egg and cress, smoked salmon with cream cheese. Crusts off.
steps: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool, then mash with mayonnaise and cress.
Butter the bread. Make 2 sandwiches with cucumber, 2 with the egg and 2 with smoked salmon on cream cheese.
Cut off the crusts and cut each into 3 fingers.
Dip the ravioli in egg, then breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil to 180°C and fry the ravioli in batches for 2 minutes until crisp and golden, then drain.
Warm the passata with salt and oregano for dipping.
Shower the ravioli with parmesan and serve.

Mickey Blue Eyes (1999).note: Clams steamed open in white wine, garlic, a pinch of chilli, parsley, olive oil.
steps: Soak the clams in salted water for 30 minutes to purge, then rinse.
Gently fry the garlic and chilli in some of the olive oil, add the clams and wine, cover and steam for 4 minutes until open.
Cook the linguine 1 minute short, finish it in the pan juices and toss with parsley and more olive oil.

Mickey Blue Eyes (1999).note: Espresso and marsala soaked biscuits, mascarpone cream, cocoa.
steps: Whisk the yolks and sugar until pale, then fold in the mascarpone.
Whip the egg whites stiff and fold into the cream.
Mix the espresso with the marsala, dip the biscuits quickly and layer with the cream in a dish.
Dust with cocoa and chill overnight.
Peel 8 long ribbons from the cucumber and curl two into each of four tall glasses, then fill with ice.
Shake the gin, cordial and lemon juice with ice for 10 seconds.
Strain over the glasses, top with soda and add a sprig of mint.

Midnight Cowboy (1969).note: On white, mustard butter, crusts off.
steps: Mash the butter with the Dijon and spread over the bread.
Fill with the ham and Swiss cheese.
Cut off the crusts, cut into quarters and wrap in baking paper.

Midnight Cowboy (1969).note: Cinnamon sugar, coffee custard to dunk.
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, egg, milk and butter into a soft dough and roll into 24 small balls.
Fry in oil at 170°C in batches until golden and cooked through. Drain.
Roll the hot doughnuts in the sugar mixed with the cinnamon.
Warm the custard with the coffee dissolved in a little hot water and serve for dipping.

Midnight Cowboy (1969).note: Butterflied, coconut and crumbs, fried golden. Sweet red pepper sauce and lime.
steps: Peel and butterfly the prawns, leaving the tails on.
Dust in flour, dip in beaten egg, then press into the panko mixed with coconut.
Fry in oil at 180°C in batches until golden. Serve with sweet chilli sauce and lime wedges.
Boil the whole oranges in water until soft.
Cool the oranges, then blitz smooth, skin and all.
Beat the eggs with the sugar, then mix in the oranges, almond meal and baking powder. Pour into a lined 22cm tin.
Bake at 180°C until set and golden. Cool in the tin.

Midnight Cowboy (1969).note: Shaken frothy with lime, over ice.
steps: Juice the limes and cut a pineapple wedge for each glass.

Shake the coconut water, pineapple juice, lime juice and coconut cream with ice until frothy. Strain into 4 ice-filled glasses, add rum on the side if you like, and garnish with pineapple and a lime wheel.

Miller's Crossing (1990).note: Chicken liver pâté, brandy, thyme, hot rye toast.
steps: Trim the livers and sear in butter for 2 minutes a side until still pink.
Add the shallots and thyme, then the brandy, and let it bubble off.
Blitz with the soft butter until silky, season and press into a dish.
Pour over the clarified butter and chill for 4 hours.
Toast the rye and serve with the pâté.

Miller's Crossing (1990).note: Twisted puff pastry, cheddar, parmesan, cayenne.
steps: Brush one sheet of pastry with egg and scatter with cheddar, parmesan and cayenne.
Lay the other sheet on top and press down. Cut into 1.5cm strips and twist each.
Bake at 220°C for 12 minutes until puffed and golden.

Miller's Crossing (1990).note: Lamb neck chops, potatoes, carrots, onions, stout.
steps: Brown the lamb in batches in oil.
Layer in a heavy pot with the onions, carrots and potatoes.
Pour over the stout and stock, cover and braise at 160°C for 2 hours until tender.
Finish with parsley.

Miller's Crossing (1990).note: Brioche, raisins soaked in the good Irish, custard.
steps: Soak the raisins in the whiskey for 30 minutes.
Butter the brioche and layer in a dish with the raisins.
Whisk the eggs, milk, cream and sugar and pour over.
Rest for 30 minutes.
Bake at 170°C until puffed and golden.

Miller's Crossing (1990).note: Irish whiskey, honey, lemon, clove, cinnamon stick.
steps: Boil the water. Cut four lemon wheels and stud each with cloves.
Into four heatproof glasses put whiskey, honey and lemon juice.
Top with the hot water and stir until the honey dissolves.
Float a studded wheel on top, add a cinnamon stick and serve hot.

Money Train (1995).note: Almonds, cashews and peanuts baked with honey, sugar, cinnamon and salt, stirred till glossy. Warm in a paper cone.
steps: Toss the nuts with the honey, sugar, cinnamon and salt until coated.
Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170°C, stirring halfway.
Keep stirring as they cool so they do not clump.

Money Train (1995).note: Butter shortbread the size of a fare, punched through the middle, brushed with gold.
steps: Beat the butter and icing sugar until pale, then mix in the flour to a soft dough.
Chill the dough for 15 minutes so it rolls cleanly.
Roll 5mm thick, cut rounds the size of a subway token and cut a small hole from the middle of each.
Bake at 160°C until just set and pale gold.
Cool on the tray, then brush with gold dust mixed with a drop of water.

Money Train (1995).note: Thighs browned hard, then set on long-grain rice cooked slow with onion, green pepper, garlic, coriander, achiote, green olives and capers. Big enough for two brothers.
steps: Brown the chicken in the oil in a wide lidded pan until golden, then set aside.
Fry the onion, capsicum, garlic and coriander in the same pan until soft.
Stir in the annatto, rice, olives, capers and stock and bring to a simmer.
Sit the chicken on top, cover and cook on low until the rice is tender.
Rest, covered, before serving.

Money Train (1995).note: Puff pastry sealed around guava paste and cream cheese, brushed with sugar syrup.
steps: Thaw the pastry, then cut each sheet into 8 squares.
Put a slice of guava paste and a little cream cheese on half the squares, cover with the rest and seal the edges with a fork.
Bake at 200°C until puffed and golden.
Simmer the sugar with the water for a few minutes to make a syrup, then brush it over the warm pastries.

Money Train (1995).note: Cold lager over ice, fresh lime, tomato juice, hot sauce and Worcestershire, chilli salt rim.
ing: 5 limes, juiced, with some cut into wedges
steps: Mix the salt and chilli powder on a plate.
Rub a lime wedge around each of 4 glass rims and dip in the chilli salt.
Add ice a good squeeze of lime juice, the tomato juice, hot sauce and Worcestershire, dividing evenly.
Top each with a cold lager, stir gently and slip the glasses into small paper bags.

Moonstruck (1987).note: From a Brooklyn baker, dimpled with olive oil and coarse salt. Cut by hand.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and warm water into a wet dough. Cover and rise for 2 hours.
Oil a 30 x 20cm tin with most of the oil, tip in the dough and stretch to the corners. Rest for 30 minutes.
Dimple deeply with oiled fingers, scatter with rosemary and flaky salt and drizzle with the remaining oil.
Bake at 230°C until deep golden.

Moonstruck (1987).note: White toast fried in butter, an egg set in a ring of red pepper, yolk soft. Late supper, after the opera.
ing: 1 red capsicum, cut in 4 thick rings
steps: Cut a hole in each slice of bread.
Melt the butter in a big pan and lay in the bread. Put a capsicum ring in each hole and crack an egg into it.
Fry until the white sets, flipping the bread once. Season.

Moonstruck (1987).note: Pounded thin, floured and sautéed, with lemon, white wine, capers and butter. Secondi served with a green salad.
steps: Slice the chicken in half horizontally and pound thin.
Dust in flour and sear in the oil and butter for 2 minutes a side, then set aside.
Add the wine, lemon juice and capers, reduce by half and swirl in the cold butter and parsley.
Return the chicken to coat.

Moonstruck (1987).note: Ricotta, sugar and orange zest in chocolate dipped shells, filled to order.
ing: 80g icing sugar, plus extra for dusting
steps: Drain the ricotta in a sieve for 2 hours.
Beat with icing sugar and orange zest, then fold in the chocolate.
Pipe into the shells just before serving and dust with icing sugar.

Moonstruck (1987).note: Shaken frothy with lemon and egg white, over ice, a cherry on top. La bella luna, every night.
steps: Shake the amaretto, lemon juice and egg white hard without ice, in rounds for two drinks at a time.
Shake again with ice.
Strain over fresh ice in four short glasses and add a cherry to each.

My Cousin Vinny (1992).note: Butter & sharp cheddar The grits cross-examination. Nobody cooks them that fast.
steps: Bring the milk, water and salt to the boil.
Whisk in the grits, then stir over low heat until creamy. It takes much longer than five minutes.
Finish with the butter and cheddar.

ing: salt and pepper, to taste (for the cornmeal)
steps: Slice the tomatoes 1cm thick, salt and leave for 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Dip in buttermilk, then in the cornmeal seasoned with salt and pepper.
Shallow-fry in the oil at 180°C for 2 minutes a side in batches.
Mix the mayonnaise, mustard, capers and hot sauce for the remoulade.

My Cousin Vinny (1992).note: Two biscuits, sausage gravy Where Vinny tries to order breakfast.
ing: 2 tbsp self-raising flour, extra for the gravy
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Grate the frozen butter into the 300g self-raising flour with a pinch of salt and toss to coat.
Stir in the buttermilk to make a soft dough, fold it over on itself three times, pat out 2cm thick and cut 8 biscuits.
Bake the biscuits on a lined tray until risen and golden.
Squeeze the sausage meat out of the skins and brown it in a frying pan, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in the extra flour for a minute, then add the milk a little at a time and simmer until thick, with plenty of black pepper. Split the biscuits and spoon the gravy over.

My Cousin Vinny (1992).note: Cream gravy, mashed potatoes Sac-O-Suds, the corner store where the whole mess started.
ing: 150g plain flour, seasoned, for the coating
2 tbsp plain flour, for the gravy
steps: For the mash: boil 920g peeled floury potatoes until soft, drain well and mash with the butter and milk.
Pound the steaks very thin.
Dredge in seasoned flour, dip in buttermilk, then flour again.
Shallow-fry 3 minutes a side until crisp.
Pour off most of the oil, stir the gravy flour into the pan, whisk in the milk and simmer thick with lots of black pepper.
Serve over the mashed potato.

My Cousin Vinny (1992).note: Warm, with pouring cream Mona Lisa's pick. Positraction, and the tyre marks to prove it.
steps: Toss the blackberries with the sugar and cornflour in a dish.
Rub the butter into the flour and the topping sugar, add the milk and drop spoonfuls on top.
Bake at 190°C for 35 minutes.
Serve with cream.

My Cousin Vinny (1992).note: By the pitcher, lemon on the side So sweet your teeth hurt.
ing: 2 ripe peaches, sliced, plus 1 for serving
steps: Simmer the peaches with the sugar and water for 10 minutes, mash lightly and strain, keeping the syrup.
Steep the tea bags in the boiling water for 5 minutes and remove.
Stir in the peach syrup and lemon juice and chill for 2 hours.
Serve over ice with fresh peach slices and mint.

Once Upon a Time in America (1984).note: Potato and sweet onion in puff pastry, hot mustard.
ing: salt and white pepper, to taste
steps: Boil the potatoes until tender, drain and mash.
Cook the onion in the butter over low heat until golden, then mix into the mash with salt and white pepper.
Cut each pastry sheet into 4 squares, fill, fold into parcels and brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 200°C until golden and puffed.
Serve with the hot mustard.

Once Upon a Time in America (1984).note: Bagel rounds, chive cream cheese, smoked salmon. The old neighbourhood, Sunday morning.
steps: Slice the bagels into thin rounds and brush with olive oil.
Bake at 180°C until crisp.
Beat the cream cheese with chives and lemon zest.
Serve the crisps with the schmear and smoked salmon on the side.

Once Upon a Time in America (1984).note: Slow braised on onions, paprika and tomato gravy. Same table as always.
steps: Season the brisket and sear hard on all sides.
Spread the onions in a roasting dish and sit the brisket on top. Pour over the stock whisked with tomato paste and paprika.
Cover and braise at 150°C for 4 hours.
Rest for 20 minutes, slice against the grain.
Boil the juices for 10 minutes to make gravy.

Once Upon a Time in America (1984).note: Sponge in a paper cup, vanilla cream piped tall, a cherry. Try not to eat it on the stairs.
steps: Cut 8 rounds of sponge to fit the bottom of the paper cups.
Whip the cream with mascarpone, icing sugar and vanilla to firm peaks.
Pipe high over the sponge in a tall swirl and top each with a cherry.
Chill for 30 minutes before serving.

Once Upon a Time in America (1984).note: Rye, lemon, sugar, egg white, a dash of bitters.
steps: Dissolve the sugar in the hot water and cool to make syrup.
Shake the whiskey, lemon juice, 40ml of the syrup and egg white without ice for 15 seconds, then with ice for 15 seconds.
Strain into four china teacups, dot the foam with bitters and serve straight away.

Planes, Trains and Automobiles (1987).note: Salted peanuts, pretzels, chocolate and beef jerky in one shared bowl. Bought before the thief cleans out the room overnight.
steps: Chop the chocolate bars into chunks.
Tip the salted peanuts, pretzels, chocolate and beef jerky into a shared bowl and mix gently.
Divide between four people for the motel snack break.

Planes, Trains and Automobiles (1987).note: Buttermilk soaked onion rings in crisp golden beer batter. Named for Del's trunk full of samples.
steps: Slice the onions into thick rings and soak in the buttermilk.
Whisk the flour, lager and salt into a batter.
Heat the oil to 185°C.
Drain the rings, dip in the batter and fry in small batches until puffed and golden.
Drain and serve hot.

Planes, Trains and Automobiles (1987).note: Roast turkey with cranberry, baked stuffing and gravy in soft buns. Neal brings Del home for Thanksgiving dinner.
steps: Dissolve the salt in the water, submerge the turkey and refrigerate for 6 hours.
Drain, pat dry and roast at 170°C until the centre reaches 70°C for 2 minutes.
Make the stuffing mix with the packet water amount, spread in a small dish and bake beside the turkey, then cut into squares.
Rest the turkey and slice.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for a minute, whisk in the stock and simmer for gravy.
Fill the buns with turkey, cranberry sauce, stuffing squares and a spoonful of gravy.

Planes, Trains and Automobiles (1987).n: Del's Wichita fried chicken and mash
Planes, Trains and Automobiles (1987).note: Crumbed chicken, creamy mash, peppery white gravy and green beans. Del knows a place in every town on the way.
ing: 2 large chicken breasts, halved and flattened
steps: Boil the potatoes until soft, then mash with half the butter and 100ml milk.
Dust the chicken in flour, dip in beaten egg and coat in breadcrumbs. Fry until golden and cooked through.
Melt the rest of the butter in the pan, stir in 2 tbsp of the flour, then whisk in the rest of the milk and the pepper for the gravy.
Boil the beans and serve with the chicken, mash and gravy.

Planes, Trains and Automobiles (1987).note: Spiced roast pumpkin custard in pastry, served with whipped cream. A plane, a train, a bus, a burnt car and a truck later.
steps: Roast the pumpkin at 200°C until soft, then puree.
Line a 20cm pie dish with the pastry and blind-bake with paper and weights at 180°C, then remove the weights and bake again.
Whisk the puree with eggs, sugar, half the cream, cinnamon, ground ginger and nutmeg.
Pour into the crust and bake at 170°C until just set.
Cool, whip the remaining cream softly and serve.

Planes, Trains and Automobiles (1987).n: Home for Thanksgiving apple cider punch
Planes, Trains and Automobiles (1987).note: Cloudy apple juice simmered with cinnamon, cloves and orange. Poured when Neal lets Del in from the snow.
steps: Put the apple juice, two cinnamon sticks, cloves, orange and sugar in a saucepan.
Simmer gently for 15 minutes without boiling.
Strain into a jug and pour into four mugs.
Add bourbon to each adult mug and serve with a fresh cinnamon stick.

Premium Rush (2012).note: Oats, dates, peanuts and seeds baked with honey, butter and brown sugar.
steps: Melt the butter, honey and brown sugar together.
Stir through the oats, dates, peanuts and seeds.
Press into a lined tin and bake at 170°C.
Cool completely before cutting into bars.

Premium Rush (2012).note: Pork neck marinated overnight in hoisin, honey, soy and five spice, roasted, in steamed buns.
steps: Mix the hoisin, honey, soy and five spice and coat the pork.
Marinate in the fridge overnight, at least 4 hours.
Roast at 200°C, basting with the marinade.
Rest the pork, then chop.
Steam the bao buns until soft and fill with the pork.

Premium Rush (2012).note: Thighs in lemon, oregano, cumin and coriander, griddled and chopped. Turmeric rice, lettuce, white and hot sauce.
steps: Marinate the chicken in the lemon juice, oregano, cumin and coriander.
Cook the rice with the turmeric.
Mix the yoghurt, mayo, vinegar, sugar and pepper into a white sauce.
Griddle the chicken until cooked through, then chop.
Serve on shredded lettuce with rice, white sauce and hot sauce.

Premium Rush (2012).note: Chocolate chip, browned butter dough rested overnight, flaky salt.
steps: Brown the butter and cool.
Beat with the sugar and egg, then mix in the flour, bicarb and choc chips.
Rest the dough overnight in the fridge.
Roll into 16 balls on lined trays.
Bake at 180°C and sprinkle with flaky salt.

Premium Rush (2012).note: Smoothie of banana, berries, oats, peanut butter and milk, blended thick. Espresso shot 75 cents.
steps: Blend the bananas, berries, oats, peanut butter and milk until completely smooth.
Add a shot of espresso for anyone riding through traffic.
Pour into four tall glasses and drink straight away.
Blanch the mushrooms in boiling water for 1 minute and drain well.
Toss with olive oil, lemon juice, garlic and parsley. Refrigerate covered overnight.
Serve on a platter with the salami, olives and artichokes.

Prizzi's Honor (1985).note: Light crisp batter, sea salt and a squeeze of lemon.
steps: Cut the zucchini into batons, pat dry and toss with 30g of the flour.
Whisk the remaining flour with the sparkling water into a light batter.
Heat the oil to 185°C and fry the battered batons in small batches for 3 minutes until crisp and golden.
Drain, season with salt and serve with lemon.

Prizzi's Honor (1985).note: Slow sausage sugo, ricotta and mozzarella, baked until blistered. The old man's favourite. Seconds are not optional.
steps: Remove the sausages from their casings and brown in the oil, breaking up the meat.
Add the onion for 5 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the passata, water and oregano and simmer gently, stirring.
Boil the ziti for 2 minutes less than the packet time and drain. Mix the ricotta with the seasoning.
Layer pasta, sugo, ricotta and mozzarella in an ovenproof dish.
Bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until blistered and rest for 10 minutes.

Prizzi's Honor (1985).note: Crackled almond cookies in icing sugar, tied in tulle.
steps: Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks in a clean bowl.
Gently fold in the almond meal, caster sugar and almond extract.
Shape into 20 small balls, roll in icing sugar and space on lined trays.
Bake at 170°C for 15 minutes until crackled and lightly golden.
Cool on the trays for 10 minutes, then move to a rack.

Prizzi's Honor (1985).note: White peach purée topped with cold prosecco.
steps: Peel and stone the peaches, blend with the lemon juice and sugar until smooth.
Chill the purée for 30 minutes.
Spoon some purée into each chilled flute and top slowly with prosecco poured down the side. Stir once and serve straight away.

Pulp Fiction (1994).note: Your waiter brings it to the car.
steps: Soak the chicken in the buttermilk and hot sauce for at least 30 minutes in the fridge.
Mix the flour, paprika, garlic powder and salt. Lift the chicken out, let it drip, then press it into the flour so it gets a shaggy coat.
Fry in oil at 175°C in batches for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden and cooked through. Drain on a rack and salt again.
Stir the honey, mustard and mayonnaise together for dipping.
Pile the chicken into paper-lined baskets with the dip and lemon wedges.
Lower the eggs into boiling water for 10 minutes, then straight into iced water.
Slice the shallots thin and fry them slowly in the oil until golden and crisp. Drain on paper.
Peel and halve the eggs. Mash the yolks with the mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar and hot sauce until smooth, and season.
Pipe or spoon the yolk back into the whites.
Dust with smoked paprika and top with crisp shallots and snipped chives.

Pulp Fiction (1994).note: Mayonnaise on the side, as in Holland. Royale with cheese? That's Paris.
ing: 1 L vegetable oil, for deep frying
steps: Cut the potatoes into thin fries.
Soak in cold water for an hour, then dry well.
Fry in oil at 140°C for 5 minutes in batches.
Rest the fries on a rack until cool.
Fry again at 190°C until crisp, salt and serve in red-checked paper boats with tomato sauce and a pot of mayonnaise, the way they do it in Holland.
Season the sirloin steaks with salt an hour ahead and leave them out of the fridge.
Bake the frozen skin-on fries at 220°C for 25 minutes until crisp.
Heat the oil in a pan until smoking and sear the steaks for 2 minutes a side until 48°C inside, then rest them for 5 minutes.
In the same pan cook the shallot and crushed peppercorns for 1 minute, add the brandy and cream and simmer for 2 minutes.
Cut the iceberg lettuce into wedges and spoon over the blue cheese mashed with the sour cream. Serve with the steaks, fries and peppercorn sauce.

Pulp Fiction (1994).note: This is a tasty burger! Jules, at Brett's.
steps: Simmer the soy, mirin and sugar until syrupy.
Grill the pineapple rings until charred.
Shape the mince into 4 thick patties.
Grill the patties, brushing with the teriyaki, then melt the cheddar on top.
Toast the buns and build with lettuce, patty and pineapple.

Pulp Fiction (1994).note: Vincent's pancakes, then Jules and Ezekiel 25:17.
steps: Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar, buttermilk and eggs until just combined.
Rest the batter for 15 minutes.
Cook ladlefuls in butter in a frying pan until bubbles set, flip and cook through, keeping the stack warm.
Grill the bacon until crisp. Stack the pancakes with butter and maple syrup, with bacon on the side.
Blend the ice cream and milk in batches, until just thick enough for a straw to stand up.
Pour into chilled glasses, top with whipped cream and a cherry.
Fill four tall glasses with ice.
Add 15ml vanilla syrup to each glass, or half a teaspoon of vanilla extract with a teaspoon of sugar syrup.
Top each with 300ml cold cola and stir once.

Quick Change (1990).note: A dozen, filled with feta beaten smooth with basil, olive oil and lemon peel.
steps: Cut the tops off the tomatoes and scoop out the seeds.
Blitz the feta with a handful of basil, the lemon zest and the oil until smooth.
Pipe into the tomatoes and top each with a small basil leaf.

Quick Change (1990).note: Oven-crisped, tossed in honey, butter, lime and sweet chilli sauce, with hot pepper flakes and coriander.
steps: Pat the wings dry and toss with the baking powder and salt.
Roast on a rack at 220°C, turning once, until crisp and cooked through.
Melt the butter with the honey, sweet chilli sauce, chilli flakes, lime zest and juice.
Toss the wings through and scatter with coriander.

Quick Change (1990).note: Roast breast, Swiss, iceberg, tomato, mayo and mustard. Wrapped to go.
steps: Split the rolls and spread with mayonnaise and mustard.
Fill with turkey, Swiss, lettuce and tomato and season.
Wrap each tightly in paper and cut in half.

Quick Change (1990).note: Jam sponge under white buttercream, with a piped face and a cherry nose.
steps: Split the sponge and fill with jam.
Beat the butter with the icing sugar and spread all over the cake.
Tint a little buttercream with the food colouring and pipe a clown face on top.
Press in the cherry for the nose.

Quick Change (1990).note: Bourbon shaken hard with fresh mint, lemon and sugar, over crushed ice.
steps: Muddle the mint leaves and lemon wedges with the syrup in a shaker.
Add the bourbon and ice and shake hard.
Double strain into 4 glasses filled with crushed ice.
Top with a sprig of mint and serve with short straws.

Raging Bull (1980).note: Whipped yolks with Dijon, crisp pancetta, smoked paprika, chives.
steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 10 minutes, then cool in iced water and peel.
Fry the pancetta in a dry pan until crisp, drain and crumble.
Halve the eggs and mash the yolks with mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper.
Pipe or spoon back into the whites. Top with pancetta, paprika and chives.

Raging Bull (1980).note: Poached and chilled, sharp tomato horseradish sauce, lemon.
steps: Poach the prawns in salted water for 2 minutes and chill in iced water.
Mix the tomato sauce with horseradish and the juice of 1 lemon.
Serve the prawns on ice with the sauce and wedges from the other lemon.

Raging Bull (1980).note: For two. Salted overnight, seared hard, basted in butter, garlic and thyme, carved off the bone.
steps: Salt the steaks and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight.
Sear in a smoking pan for 3 minutes a side, then add butter, garlic and thyme and baste until 52°C inside.
Rest for 8 minutes.
Slice off the bone to share.

Raging Bull (1980).note: Lemon, vanilla, icing sugar. No weigh-in tonight.
steps: Drain the ricotta for 2 hours.
Beat with sugar, eggs, lemon zest and vanilla.
Pour into a lined 22cm springform tin and bake at 160°C for 60 minutes.
Cool in the oven with the door ajar, then dust with icing sugar.

Raging Bull (1980).note: Golden rum, orange, pineapple, lime and grenadine on crushed ice.
steps: Stir the rum, juices and grenadine in a jug and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Fill four tall glasses with crushed ice and pour the punch over.
Finish each with an orange slice and a cherry on a pick.

Ratatouille (2007).note: Leek, potato and cream. Remy fixed it.
steps: Sweat the leeks in the butter over low heat until soft.
Add the potatoes and stock and simmer until the potato is very tender.
Blend silky smooth with the cream and season.
Serve topped with chives and white pepper. Anyone can cook.
Remove the mushroom stems.
Mix the gruyère with the thyme and garlic and fill the caps.
Drizzle with oil and roast at 220°C until bubbling.
Rest a few minutes before serving.
Take the salted butter out of the fridge so it is soft at room temperature.
Warm the baguettes in a 200°C oven for 6 minutes until the crust crackles when you squeeze it.
Split each baguette lengthways and spread thickly with the butter.
Fill with folds of the ham and slices of brie, close and cut into short lengths to share.

Ratatouille (2007).note: Zucchini, eggplant, squash, tomato. Takes Ego home.
steps: Cook the capsicum, onion, garlic and 2 chopped tomatoes into a soft sauce and spread it in a baking dish.
Slice the zucchini, eggplant, squash and remaining tomatoes thin and layer them in a spiral over the sauce.
Drizzle with thyme infused oil and cover with baking paper.
Bake covered at 140°C until completely tender.
Rest briefly before serving.

Ratatouille (2007).note: Veal sweetbreads in butter and lemon. The recipe Remy rewrote.
steps: Soak the veal sweetbreads in cold water in the fridge for 2 hours.
Simmer the sweetbreads in salted water for 4 minutes, then plunge into iced water and peel off the membrane.
Press the sweetbreads under a weighted tray in the fridge for an hour.
Slice into 2cm pieces, season with salt, dust with the flour and pan-fry in 30g of the butter for 3 minutes a side until golden.
Deglaze the pan with the chicken stock and lemon juice, reduce by half, then swirl in the remaining 20g cold butter and spoon the sauce over the sweetbreads.

ing: 100g caster sugar, plus extra for the tops
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C. Split the vanilla bean, scrape the seeds into the cream and warm it with the pod until it just steams.
Whisk the yolks and 100g caster sugar until pale, then pour in the warm cream slowly, whisking, and strain into a jug.
Pour into 4 ramekins in a baking dish, fill the dish with hot water halfway up the ramekins and bake until set with a slight wobble.
Cool, then chill at least 3 hours.
Sprinkle each top with a thin layer of caster sugar and torch, or grill close to the element, until it cracks like glass.

Ratatouille (2007).note: Grape juice, berries and soda. Ego's order.
ing: 4 thyme sprigs, plus extra to serve
steps: Lightly crush the blackberries with the thyme and honey in a jug.
Add the grape juice and lemon juice and stir.
Chill for 30 minutes, then strain.
Pour into stemmed glasses over ice, top with sparkling water and garnish with thyme and a blackberry.

Road to Perdition (2002).note: Sharp cheddar on white, fried crisp in butter, cut in fingers. Bread and butter pickles.
steps: Thinly slice the cucumbers and onion.
Heat the vinegar, water, sugar, salt and mustard seeds until dissolved, then pour over the vegetables.
Let the pickles cool and sit while you make the sandwiches.
Butter the bread on the outside and fill with the cheddar.
Fry over medium heat until golden on both sides. Cut into fingers and serve with the pickles.

Road to Perdition (2002).note: Warm buttermilk loaf, salted butter, cheddar.
steps: Mix the flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt, add the buttermilk and bring together into a round. Cut a deep cross on top.
Bake at 220°C.
Reduce the oven to 200°C and bake until golden and hollow when tapped. Serve warm with the butter and cheddar.

Road to Perdition (2002).note: Simmered all day and sliced thick. Buttered cabbage, carrots, boiled potatoes, hot mustard.
steps: Peel the onion, potatoes and carrots and cut the potatoes and carrots into chunks. Quarter the cabbage.
Cover the corned silverside with water in a large pot with the onion, bay leaves and peppercorns and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer the corned silverside gently, topping up the water as needed.
Add the potatoes and carrots and keep simmering.
Add the cabbage for the last of the cooking.
Slice the corned silverside thick and serve with the vegetables, butter and mustard.

Road to Perdition (2002).note: Deep dish, cinnamon apples, sharp cheddar melted on top. Michael, eat your pie.
steps: Peel, core and slice the apples. Cook them gently with the sugar and cinnamon for 5 minutes, then cool.
Line a deep pie dish with one pastry sheet, fill with the apples, cover with the second sheet and cut slits in the top.
Bake at 190°C until golden.
Lay the cheddar on top for the last stretch of baking so it melts.

Road to Perdition (2002).note: Brown sugar, soft cream, Irish style. Strictly medicinal.
steps: Whip the cream to soft ribbons so it just holds its shape. Brew the coffee.
Warm 4 heatproof glasses with hot water and tip it out.
Add brown sugar, whiskey and coffee to each glass and stir until dissolved.
Float the cream on top over the back of a spoon. Do not stir.

Saturday Night Fever (1977).note: Grilled Italian sausage in bites, soft sweet peppers and onion, a splash of red wine vinegar.
steps: Grill the sausages until cooked through and slice into chunks.
Fry the capsicums and onions in oil until soft and sweet.
Toss with the sausage and a splash of red wine vinegar.

Saturday Night Fever (1977).note: Crisp-cut potatoes under hot beef gravy and melted mozzarella. For after the last dance.
steps: Cut the potatoes into fries, soak for 30 minutes and dry well.
Fry in the oil at 150°C for 6 minutes, then at 190°C until crisp.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for a minute, whisk in the stock and simmer for 5 minutes into gravy.
Pile the fries on a tray, pour over the gravy, top with mozzarella and grill for a minute.

Saturday Night Fever (1977).note: Thin New York pie, tomato, oregano and mozzarella. Stack, fold, strut down 86th Street.
steps: Rest the dough at room temperature for an hour.
Blend the tomatoes with salt and oregano. Stretch each base thin, spread with sauce and scatter with mozzarella.
Bake on a preheated tray at the oven's highest setting.
Cut into big slices, stack two and fold.

Saturday Night Fever (1977).note: Butter cake rolled with cream cheese, dipped in white chocolate and silver dragées, on a stick.
steps: Crumble the cake and mix with the cream cheese until it holds together. Roll into 16 balls.
Chill for 30 minutes.
Push a stick into each, dip in melted white chocolate and roll in cachous.
Stand in a glass to set.

Saturday Night Fever (1977).note: Blended whisky shaken with lemon and sugar, topped with lemonade and soda over ice. A lemon wheel.
steps: Dissolve the sugar in the hot water and cool.
Shake the whisky, lemon juice and 40ml of the syrup with ice for 10 seconds.
Strain into four ice-filled highballs, top with lemonade and soda, stir once and add a lemon wheel.

Scarface (1983).note: Serrano ham béchamel, crumbed and fried golden. Lime.
steps: Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 2 minutes, then whisk in the warm milk and cook until very thick.
Stir in the ham and nutmeg, spread on a tray, cover and chill overnight.
Roll into 16 logs, dip in egg and then breadcrumbs.
Fry in the oil at 180°C in batches until golden and serve with lime.

Scarface (1983).note: Green plantain fried twice, smashed flat, garlic and lime mojo.
steps: Peel the plantains and cut into 3cm chunks.
Fry at 160°C for 4 minutes until soft.
Smash flat with a heavy glass and fry again at 190°C until crisp.
Mix the garlic, lime juice and olive oil, spoon over and finish with flaky salt.

Scarface (1983).note: Flank steak shredded into peppers, tomato, olives. Rice, beans.
steps: Simmer the steak with the bay leaves and half an onion in water until tender. Shred it and keep 250ml of the broth.
Fry the sliced onion, capsicums and garlic in olive oil until soft.
Add the cumin, oregano, tomatoes, olives, beef and broth and simmer.
Cook the rice and warm the black beans, and serve alongside.

Scarface (1983).note: Puff pastry, guava paste and cream cheese, sugar crust.
steps: Cut the pastry sheets into 8 squares in all.
Put a slice of guava paste and a teaspoon of cream cheese in the middle of 4 squares.
Cover with the other squares, press the edges with a fork, brush with egg and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 200°C until puffed.

Scarface (1983).note: White rum, lime and mint over crushed ice, soda on top.
steps: Dissolve the sugar in the hot water and cool to make syrup.
In each tall glass, gently muddle mint with some syrup and lime juice.
Add rum, fill with crushed ice, top with soda and stir.

Serpico (1973).note: Toasted and spread thick with cream cheese, smoked salmon, capers, red onion and fresh dill.
steps: Split and toast the bagels.
Spread each half thickly with cream cheese, then top with smoked salmon, capers, onion and small sprigs of dill. Cut each half in two to share.

Serpico (1973).note: Steamed soft, hand sliced, piled high, with mustard and a pickle.
steps: Steam the pastrami in a covered colander over simmering water until hot and soft.
Spread the rye with mustard, pile the pastrami high on half the slices and close. Cut in half and serve with a pickle each.

Serpico (1973).note: Steamed pastrami, Swiss, slaw and Russian dressing on a long roll.
steps: Steam the pastrami until glossy.
Mix the mayonnaise, tomato sauce, horseradish and pickle for Russian dressing.
Toss the coleslaw mix with half the dressing.
Fill the rolls with pastrami, Swiss cheese, slaw and the rest of the dressing.

Serpico (1973).note: Soft sour cream cake cookie, iced half vanilla, half chocolate.
steps: Beat the butter and sugar, add the egg, sour cream and vanilla, then mix in the flour and baking powder.
Scoop 12 mounds onto lined trays.
Bake at 180°C until set, then cool completely.
Make a thick icing with the icing sugar and a little hot water. Ice half of each flat side, then stir the cocoa into the rest and ice the other half.

Serpico (1973).note: Dark roast steeped overnight in the icebox, vanilla syrup, milk and a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
steps: Stir the coffee into the cold water the night before and refrigerate.
Steep for 12 hours, then strain through a paper filter.
Simmer the sugar with the syrup water and vanilla and cool.
Fill 4 glasses with ice and add coffee, syrup and milk to each. Top with a small scoop of ice cream.

She's All That (1999).note: Falafel in warm pita with tahini, served by Laney in the falafel hat.
ing: 2 x 400g tins of chickpeas, drained and patted dry
steps: Pulse the chickpeas, onion, garlic, parsley, cumin, flour and salt to a coarse paste and roll into 16 balls.
Fry in hot oil in batches until deep brown and crisp.
Whisk the tahini with lemon juice, salt and water until pourable.
Warm the pita, fill with falafel and tomato and drizzle with tahini.

She's All That (1999).note: Black bean and cheddar nachos, loaded for the Real World party.
steps: Warm the beans with the paprika, cumin, a splash of water and salt, crushing a few.
Mash the avocados with the lime juice and salt.
Layer the chips, beans and cheddar on a tray and bake at 200°C until the cheese melts.
Top with salsa, guacamole, sour cream and jalapenos and serve straight away.

She's All That (1999).note: Meatball and provolone rolls, kept well clear of the hacky sack act.
steps: Mix the mince, crumbs, egg, parmesan, half the garlic and salt, and roll into 20 balls.
Brown the meatballs in a hot pan.
Add the passata, oregano and the rest of the garlic and simmer until thick.
Split the rolls, fill with meatballs and sauce, top with provolone and grill until melted.
Tuck in the basil and serve.

She's All That (1999).note: Grilled fish in soft tortillas with lime slaw, for the beach day Laney says yes to.
steps: Rub the fish with the spices, oil and salt.
Toss the cabbage with the juice of 2 limes and salt, and stir the chipotle into the sour cream.
Grill the fish until just flaking, then break into chunks.
Warm the tortillas and fill with slaw, fish, chipotle cream, coriander and lime.

She's All That (1999).n: Red dress on the stairs strawberry shortcake
She's All That (1999).note: Berry shortcake with cream, red as the dress on the stairs.
ing: 60g caster sugar, plus 2 tbsp for the berries
steps: Toss the strawberries with 2 tbsp sugar and leave to go juicy.
Rub the butter into the flour and 60g sugar, stir in the buttermilk and pat out 3cm thick.
Cut 4 rounds and bake at 210°C until golden.
Whip the cream with the vanilla, split the shortcakes and fill with berries and cream.

She's All That (1999).note: Pineapple and cranberry punch from the prom, foghorn for Dean.
steps: Stir the pineapple and cranberry juices together in a punch bowl.
Add the lime slices, frozen raspberries and ice.
Top with lemonade just before serving.

Sleepless in Seattle (1993).note: Hot-smoked fish worked into cream cheese and crème fraîche with dill, capers, lemon and horseradish. Toasted bagel chips. Flown in overnight from Seattle.
steps: Flake the salmon into the cream cheese and crème fraîche.
Add lemon juice, dill, capers and horseradish and mix.
Slice the bagels thin and brush with oil.
Bake at 180°C into crisp chips.
Serve the chips with the dip.

Sleepless in Seattle (1993).note: Popped in coconut oil, tossed with browned butter and sea salt.
steps: Cook the butter until nutty and golden.
Heat the coconut oil with 3 kernels in a lidded pot.
Add the rest of the kernels once they pop, cover and shake until popping slows.
Toss with the brown butter and flaky salt.

Sleepless in Seattle (1993).note: Fillet roasted under parsley, grated lemon peel and bread crumbs. Steamed green beans, warm butter spooned over. Mild. Nothing to sneeze at.
steps: Mix the breadcrumbs with parsley, lemon zest and oil.
Press onto the salmon and roast at 200°C.
Steam the beans.
Melt the butter with the lemon juice and spoon over everything.

Sleepless in Seattle (1993).note: Browned butter sugar cookies, hand cut, iced red and white.
steps: Brown the butter and cool.
Beat with the sugar and whole egg, then mix in the flour.
Roll to 5mm and cut into hearts.
Bake at 180°C.
Cool completely.
Mix the icing sugar with the egg white. Tint half red and ice the cookies.

Sleepless in Seattle (1993).note: Strong coffee with dark chocolate melted through, cold milk over ice, whipped cream and cocoa. The way they take it in Seattle.
steps: Stir the hot coffee with the chocolate and sugar until melted.
Cool.
Whip the cream.
Fill 4 glasses with ice and add the mocha and milk.
Top with whipped cream and dust with cocoa.

Spider-Man (2002).note: Two fried eggs, melted American and hot sauce, wrapped in foil on a soft roll.
steps: Split the rolls and toast lightly.
Fry the eggs in the butter, breaking the yolks, and lay two slices of cheese over each pair to melt.
Stack the eggs into the rolls with salt, pepper and a dash of hot sauce.
Wrap each roll in foil for a couple of minutes so it all steams together.

Spider-Man (2002).note: Warm turkey, cranberry sauce and crisp baked stuffing on toasted mini buns.
steps: Make the stuffing mix as the packet says and press into a tray.
Bake at 190°C until crisp, then cut into 8 squares.
Toast the roll buns and warm the turkey. Fill each bun with turkey, cranberry sauce and a square of stuffing.

Spider-Man (2002).note: Brined roast turkey breast, stuffing, pan gravy, roast potatoes and pumpkin.
steps: Stir the salt into the water and brine the turkey breast, covered, in the fridge.
Brine the turkey overnight.
Pat the turkey dry, rub with butter and cut the potatoes and pumpkin into chunks.
Roast the turkey at 170°C until 70°C inside, with the potato and pumpkin roasting alongside.
Rest the turkey, covered. Bake the stuffing mix as the packet says.
Make gravy from the pan juices, flour and stock. Slice the turkey and serve with everything.

Spider-Man (2002).note: Fluffy pancakes cooked in butter, piled high, with warm maple syrup.
steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. Add the eggs, buttermilk and some melted butter.
Rest the batter.
Cook ladlefuls in a buttered pan over medium heat until bubbles set, then flip. Keep the stack warm.
Stack high and pour over the maple syrup.

Spider-Man (2002).note: Fresh lime, sweet red syrup and soda water over ice, a maraschino on top.
steps: Squeeze 4 limes and cut the last into wedges.
Into each of 4 tall glasses of ice pour the lime juice and cherry syrup, top with soda water, stir once and drop in a cherry and a lime wedge.

Spider-Man 2 (2004).note: Six knots of our dough, baked golden, tossed in garlic butter and parsley.
steps: Cut the dough into 8 strips and tie into knots.
Cover on a lined tray and prove until puffy.
Bake at 230°C until golden.
Melt the butter with the garlic over low heat, then toss the hot knots in the garlic butter and parsley.

Spider-Man 2 (2004).note: Potato and fried onion in thin pastry, baked golden. Yellow mustard.
steps: Peel and boil the potatoes until tender, then drain.
Fry the onion in the butter until soft. Mash the potatoes with the onion, salt and pepper.
Cut each pastry sheet into 4 squares, put a mound of potato on each, fold up and pinch closed.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 200°C until golden. Serve hot with yellow mustard.

Spider-Man 2 (2004).note: Thin crisp crust, crushed tomato, mozzarella, cupping pepperoni.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and water, then knead for about 8 minutes. Divide into 2 balls.
Cold-ferment the covered balls in the fridge for 24 hours (up to 48 is fine).
Bring the dough to room temperature for 2 hours.
Heat a pizza steel in the oven at its maximum temperature, about 250 to 275°C.
Stretch each ball thin, spread with half the tomatoes and top with half the mozzarella and pepperoni. Bake one at a time on the hot steel until the crust is cooked and crisp. Cut into wedges.

Spider-Man 2 (2004).note: Buttermilk stack cooked in butter, maple syrup. Like your aunt makes.
steps: Separate the eggs. Mix the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt.
Whisk the yolks with the buttermilk and fold into the flour. Whip the whites to soft peaks and fold through gently.
Cook eight small pancakes in batches in a little butter over medium heat, until bubbles set, then flip and cook briefly.
Stack two per person and serve with maple syrup.

Spider-Man 2 (2004).note: Strong coffee on ice, milk, vanilla ice cream.
steps: Stir the coffee and cold water together in a jar and cover.
Steep in the fridge for 12 hours (up to 18).
Strain through a coffee filter.
Divide the ice between four glasses, add iced coffee and milk to each, then top with ice cream.

Splash (1984).note: On crushed ice, shallot and red wine vinegar mignonette, cracked pepper. Half a dozen, with lemon. Up from the Cape daily.
steps: Mix the shallots, vinegar and plenty of cracked pepper. Rest to let the flavours settle.
Shuck the oysters, keeping the liquor in the shell.
Lay the oysters on crushed ice with lemon wedges and the mignonette in a small bowl with a spoon.

Splash (1984).note: Cod in a cold lager batter, thick potatoes done twice. Tartar sauce and lemon. Served in a paper cone at the oyster bar.
steps: Whisk the flour, cornflour and lager to a batter.
Cut the potatoes into chips, rinse and dry them.
Fry the chips in the oil twice, first at a lower heat, then hot to crisp.
Dip the cod strips in batter and fry in the oil at 180°C until golden.
Serve in paper cones with tartare and lemon.

Splash (1984).note: About 1¾ lb from our tank, split, brushed with garlic butter and finished under the grill. Drawn butter and lemon. Most guests leave the shell.
steps: Boil the lobsters in salted water, allowing about 8 minutes per 500g of weight.
Melt half the butter with the garlic. Keep the rest for drawn butter.
Split the lobsters lengthways and crack the claws. Brush the flesh with the garlic butter.
Grill flesh-side up until hot and lightly golden.
Serve with drawn butter and lemon.

Splash (1984).note: Coconut cream set firm under a clear sea-blue layer, gummy fish on top.
steps: Bloom 3 gelatine leaves in cold water and stir into the warm coconut milk with half the sugar.
Pour into four glasses and chill until set.
Steep the pea flowers in the hot water with the remaining sugar, strain, and stir in 3 bloomed gelatine leaves.
Cool to room temperature, then pour over the set coconut layer.
Chill until firm, then top with gummy fish.

Splash (1984).note: Vodka and blue curaçao over ice, topped with lemon-lime soda and a lemon wheel. Must be 19 to order.
steps: Fill four tall glasses with ice.
Add vodka and blue curaçao to each.
Top with lemonade, stir gently and garnish with a lemon wheel.

Taxi Driver (1976).note: Cooked twice in hot oil until crisp, salted hard. White vinegar on every table.
steps: Cut the potatoes into thick fries, rinse and dry well.
Fry in oil at 140°C until pale and soft, in batches.
Rest the fries on a rack.
Fry again at 185°C until crisp and golden. Salt hard and put the vinegar on the table.

Taxi Driver (1976).note: Thick slabs of the sharp stuff, dill spears, a sleeve of crackers and hot English mustard.
steps: Take the cheddar out of the fridge an hour ahead.
Cut the cheddar into thick slabs and the pickles into spears. Lay out with the crackers and a small dish of mustard for smearing.

Taxi Driver (1976).note: Rare slices warmed in brown gravy on thick white toast, more gravy poured over. Buttered mashed potatoes and peas.
steps: Peel and boil the potatoes until soft, then mash with the butter.
Cook the peas and toss with butter.
Warm the beef in the hot gravy.
Toast the bread, lay on plates, pile on the beef and pour over more gravy. Serve with the mash and peas.

Taxi Driver (1976).note: Buttered white loaf layered with brandied peaches, baked in vanilla custard. Served warm.
steps: Soak the peaches in the brandy and brown sugar.
Butter the bread and layer with the peaches in a baking dish.
Whisk the eggs with the milk and vanilla and pour over.
Rest so the bread soaks up the custard.
Bake at 170°C until set and golden. Serve warm.

Taxi Driver (1976).note: Strong drip with a nip of peach brandy and brown sugar, a spoonful of soft whipped cream on top. Twelve hours on coffee is no way to drive.
steps: Brew the coffee strong using the water.
Lightly whip the cream until just thick.
Put brown sugar and peach brandy into 4 diner mugs, pour in hot coffee and stir. Spoon a little cream on top and serve straight away.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1990).note: A dozen pinwheels: dough, red sauce, pepperoni, mozzarella. Baked golden.
steps: Roll the dough into a thin rectangle and spread with the sauce.
Cover with the pepperoni and mozzarella, roll up tightly from the long side, slice into 12 rounds and place cut side up on a lined tray.
Bake at 220°C until golden.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1990).note: Fresh mozzarella torn over charred sourdough, honey, basil.
steps: Take the fresh mozzarella out of the fridge to lose its chill.
Warm the honey with the chilli flakes until runny.
Brush the sourdough with oil and char on a hot grill pan, 2 minutes a side.
Tear the fresh mozzarella over the toast, spoon the honey chilli over, crack pepper on top and add the basil.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1990).note: Thick-cut pepperoni, mozzarella, red sauce. Chilli flakes at the table. “I have always liked… Cowabunga.” Splinter
steps: Divide the dough in two and stretch each thin on an oiled tray.
Spread with the sauce, scatter the mozzarella and cover with the pepperoni.
Bake at the oven's highest setting until the edges char and the pepperoni curls into cups.
Warm the honey with the chilli flakes and pour over at the table with the basil.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1990).note: Chocolate chip dough baked in a pie tin, chocolate drizzle, candy.
steps: Beat the butter, sugar and egg, then mix in the flour, bicarb and choc chips.
Press into a greased pizza tray and bake at 180°C.
Drizzle with melted chocolate, scatter the lollies and cut into wedges.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1990).note: Fresh-pressed Granny Smiths, lime juice, club soda, over ice.
steps: Blend the apples with the lime juice and 200ml water, then strain.
Pour over ice in 4 glasses and top with soda water.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles II: The Sec.note: Charred green chilli, avocado, lime, coriander. Warm corn chips. Glows a little. Scooped to order.
steps: Char the chillies until blackened, then peel, seed and chop.
Mash the avocados with the lime juice and salt, then fold in the chilli, onion and coriander.
Press cling wrap on the surface until serving. Warm the corn chips.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles II: The Sec.note: Six split minis, red sauce, bubbling mozzarella, pepperoni. Nobody stops at one.
steps: Split the bagels and spread with the sauce.
Top with the mozzarella and pepperoni.
Grill until bubbling.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles II: The Sec.note: Bitter greens, shaved parmesan, lemon, crisp garlic crumbs. TGRI found them growing by the leak.
steps: Fry 60g fresh breadcrumbs in 2 tbsp olive oil with 1 crushed garlic clove until crisp.
Whisk the juice of 1 lemon with 3 tbsp olive oil and salt.
Toss 200g dandelion greens or rocket with the dressing, scatter 40g shaved parmesan and the crumbs.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles II: The Sec.note: Thin crust, tomato, mozzarella, pepperoni, fresh pineapple, jalapeño. The pie Keno used to get in the door at April's.
steps: Stretch the dough thin on an oiled tray and spread with the sauce.
Scatter the mozzarella, pepperoni, pineapple and sliced jalapeño.
Bake at the oven's highest setting until the edges char.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles II: The Sec.note: Beef and parmesan meatballs, red sauce, melted mozzarella, toasted roll.
steps: Mix 500g beef mince with 1 egg, 40g breadcrumbs and 30g grated parmesan, roll into 16 balls and brown in olive oil.
Add 400ml pizza sauce and simmer 15 minutes.
Split 4 sub rolls, fill with the meatballs and sauce, lay on 200g sliced mozzarella and grill until melted.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles II: The Sec.note: Buttermilk doughnuts, fried golden, sharp lime glaze. Perry's antidote, hidden in doughnuts for Tokka and Rahzar.
steps: Whisk the dry ingredients, then beat in the buttermilk, egg and melted butter to a soft dough.
Pat out 1.5cm thick and cut 12 rings.
Fry at 175°C, 2 minutes a side, and drain.
Mix the icing sugar with lime zest and juice, dip the warm doughnuts and let the glaze set.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles II: The Sec.note: Kiwifruit, lime and honey blitzed with ice and lemonade. A safe batch.
steps: Peel and chop the kiwifruit.
Blend the kiwi with the lime juice, honey and ice until slushy.
Add the lemonade and pulse twice. Pour into 4 glasses, add a lime wheel and serve with thick straws.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles III (1993).note: Rice balls brushed with miso and soy, grilled crisp, wrapped in nori. Four guards went to New York. Four turtles came back in their armour.
steps: Cook the rice and cool until you can handle it.
With wet salted hands, press into 8 firm triangles.
Mix the miso, soy and sugar.
Grill the onigiri 4 minutes a side until crisp, brushing with the glaze at the end, then wrap the base in nori.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles III (1993).note: Chicken thigh and spring onion, basted with soy and honey tare. “Uh, o-hi-o, wasabi.” Donatello, blending in.
steps: Simmer the soy, honey and rice vinegar until syrupy.
Cut the chicken and spring onions and thread onto soaked skewers.
Grill over high heat, turning and basting with the tare at the end.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles III (1993).note: Eggplant grilled soft, sweet miso and sesame on top. Grilled while Donatello builds a second sceptre. It doesn't go well.
steps: Halve 2 eggplants lengthways, score the flesh and brush with 2 tbsp vegetable oil.
Grill cut side down for 8 minutes, turn and cook 8 minutes more until soft.
Mix 3 tbsp white miso, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tbsp water, spread over the cut sides and grill until bubbling.
Scatter with toasted sesame seeds.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles III (1993).note: Chicken, daikon, shiitake, cabbage and tofu in kombu dashi, rice on the side. Sixty hours to get home. Time for one hotpot.
steps: Soak the kombu in 1.5L water, bring to a simmer and lift it out. Add the soy and honey.
Simmer the daikon until starting to soften.
Add the chicken and simmer.
Add the shiitake, cabbage and tofu, cook through and finish with spring onions. Serve at the table with rice.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles III (1993).note: Buckwheat noodles in hot soy dashi, spring onion, a soft egg. Kenshin got sent the other way, to New York.
steps: Bring 1.2L dashi to a simmer with 4 tbsp soy sauce and 2 tbsp mirin.
Soft boil 4 eggs for 6 minutes and peel.
Cook 360g dried soba for 4 minutes, rinse and divide between 4 bowls.
Pour the hot broth over, add a halved egg to each and scatter sliced spring onions.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles III (1993).note: Soft rice dumplings rolled in roasted soybean flour, dark brown sugar syrup. Save one for Splinter's Elvis at the end.
steps: Simmer the brown sugar with 80ml water until syrupy and cool.
Mix the rice flour with water to a soft dough and roll into 24 dimpled balls.
Boil until they float, 1 minute more, then into iced water.
Roll in kinako and sugar, skewer and pour the syrup over.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles III (1993).note: Roasted barley steeped and chilled. Nutty and clean. “I told you these disguises weren't gonna work!” Raphael
steps: Toast the barley in a dry pan until dark golden.
Simmer in 1.5L water, cool, strain and chill.
Serve over ice.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant May.note: Crisp underneath, then steamed. Soy and black vinegar. From the supply run. Splinter only lets them up top for that.
steps: Mix the pork, chives, ginger, half the soy and the sesame oil.
Fill, pleat and seal the wrappers.
Fry until the bases are golden, add water, cover and steam.
Mix the rest of the soy with the black vinegar for dipping.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant May.note: Beef smashed thin, American cheese, pickles, plenty of tomato sauce. Molly-whopped. Ketchup everywhere.
steps: Roll the mince into 8 balls.
Smash flat in a smoking hot pan, season and cook until the edges crust.
Flip, add cheese and cook 1 minute more.
Serve on toasted buns with pickles, onion, mustard and tomato sauce.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant May.note: Thick fries, beef chilli, melted cheddar, jalapeños. Leatherhead says g'day, then takes the big bowl.
steps: Bake 1kg frozen thick fries at 220°C for 25 minutes.
Brown 300g beef mince with 1 diced onion and 2 tsp chilli powder, add a 400g tin kidney beans and 200ml passata and simmer 15 minutes.
Spoon over the fries, top with 150g grated cheddar, melt under the grill and finish with sliced jalapeños and spring onion.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant May.note: Thin New York pie, pepperoni, mozzarella, pickled jalapeños, ranch drizzle. “Can we explain this over some pizza?” Michelangelo
steps: Stretch the dough thin on an oiled tray and spread with the sauce.
Scatter the mozzarella, pepperoni and oregano.
Bake at the oven's highest setting.
Scatter the jalapeños over the hot pie, drizzle with ranch and cut into big slices.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant May.note: Italian sausage, mushroom, bell pepper, red onion, olives. Everything on it. Whale-sized, like Superfly after the zoo.
steps: Divide 1kg pizza dough in two and stretch thin.

Spread each with 125ml passata and a pinch of oregano, scatter 400g grated mozzarella between them and top with 300g crumbled Italian sausage, 150g sliced mushrooms, 1 sliced green capsicum, 1 sliced red onion and a handful of black olives.
Bake at the oven's highest setting for 12 minutes.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant May.note: Vanilla cupcakes, bright green buttercream piped in drips. Stockman just wanted a family. Here's to Dad.
steps: Beat the butter and sugar, add the eggs, then fold in the flour and milk.
Divide between 12 cases and bake at 180°C.
Beat the butter, icing sugar and colouring until fluffy and pipe on in drips once cool.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant May.note: Cherry cola over vanilla ice cream, a maraschino cherry on top. The canister that turned Superfly back into a pile of animals.
steps: Scoop the ice cream into 4 tall glasses.
Slowly pour the cola over and top with a cherry.

The Adjustment Bureau (2011).note: Almonds, cashews and pecans glazed with honey, butter and cinnamon.
steps: Melt the butter with the honey, sugar, cinnamon and salt.
Toss through the nuts, spread on a lined tray and roast at 170°C, stirring halfway.
Cool so they crisp, then pour into paper cones.

The Adjustment Bureau (2011).note: Toasted baguette, whipped chèvre, warm honey, thyme and cracked pepper.
steps: Cut the baguette into 8 slices and toast at 200°C until golden.
Beat the goat's cheese with the cream until light.
Warm the honey gently.
Spread the cheese on the toast, drizzle with honey and finish with thyme and pepper.

The Adjustment Bureau (2011).note: Seared sirloin, shallot and red wine butter, double-fried potatoes.
steps: Simmer the shallots with the wine until almost dry. Cool, then mix into the butter with the salt and chill.
Cut the potatoes into frites, rinse and dry thoroughly.
Fry in oil at 140°C, then drain and cool.
Fry again at 185°C until crisp. Salt lightly.
Season the steaks and sear hard in a hot pan with the oil to your preferred doneness.
Rest the steaks, then slice and top with the shallot red wine butter. Serve with frites.

The Adjustment Bureau (2011).note: Dark chocolate, baked to order, set at the edges, soft in the centre.
ing: 145g butter, plus extra for the moulds
steps: Butter four 150ml moulds. Heat the oven to 200°C.
Melt the chocolate with the butter gently and cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs, yolks and sugar until pale. Stir in the chocolate mixture, then fold in the flour.
Divide among the moulds and bake until the edges are set and centres stay soft.
Rest briefly, loosen the edges and turn onto plates. Serve immediately.

The Adjustment Bureau (2011).note: Gin, lemon and sugar, shaken, topped with brut champagne. Cash bar. Drink tickets welcome.
steps: Dissolve the sugar in the hot water and cool.
Shake the gin, lemon juice and cooled syrup with ice.
Strain evenly into 4 chilled flutes and top each with champagne, pouring slowly.
Finish with a long strip of lemon peel.

The Big Lebowski (1998).note: Charred yoghurt flatbread striped with sesame and oregano, feta dip, pomegranate, mint and dill. Laid out like the rug that really tied the room together.
steps: Mix the flour, 250g of the yoghurt and the salt into a soft dough, knead for 1 minute, then rest 10 minutes.
Whip the feta with the remaining 100g yoghurt, the lemon zest and juice and 2 tbsp of the olive oil until smooth.
Divide the dough into 4 and roll each piece into a thin rectangle about 25cm long.
Cook each flatbread in a hot dry frying pan for 2 minutes a side, until puffed and charred in spots.
Brush with the rest of the olive oil and sprinkle the sesame and oregano seeds in stripes across each one, like a rug.
Spread the feta dip on a platter, lay the flatbreads alongside and scatter with the pomegranate, mint and dill.

The Big Lebowski (1998).note: Corn tortillas rolled round chorizo, potato and cheddar, fried crisp, with purple pickled onion, lime crema and salsa verde. Rolled tight and dressed in purple. Nobody messes with the Jesus.
steps: Toss the onion with the vinegar, sugar and half the salt and leave it to turn purple while you cook.
Boil the potatoes in water with the rest of the salt for 10 minutes until tender, then drain.
Fry the chorizo, broken up, in a dry pan for 6 minutes, add the cumin and potatoes and crush together, then stir in the cheddar.
Warm the tortillas in the microwave under a damp tea towel for 1 minute so they roll without cracking.
Spoon the filling along each tortilla, roll tightly and hold with a toothpick.
Shallow fry the taquitos in 1cm of hot oil, seam side down first, for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until crisp. Drain on paper towel.
Mix the sour cream with the lime zest and juice. Serve the taquitos with the lime crema, salsa verde, pickled onion and coriander.

The Big Lebowski (1998).note: Crisp oven-roasted chicken wings in a hot sauce, honey and butter glaze, spring onion, pickled cucumber. “This is not 'Nam. This is bowling. There are rules.” Walter.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Pat the wings dry and toss with the baking powder and salt.
Roast the wings on a rack over a lined tray for 40 to 45 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden.
While they roast, simmer the hot sauce, honey, soy sauce, 1 tbsp of the rice vinegar, the sesame oil and garlic in a small pan for 2 minutes until glossy.
Slice the cucumber thinly and toss with the rest of the rice vinegar.
Toss the hot wings in the glaze and scatter with the sesame seeds and spring onion. Serve with the cucumber.

The Big Lebowski (1998).note: Two smashed beef patties seared in mustard, American cheese, slow-cooked onion, pickles and spread on a toasted bun. Fries on the side. The drive-thru order, three in the car. “Those are good burgers, Walter.” Donny.
steps: Cut the potatoes into thin fries, rinse well and pat completely dry.
Fry the fries in the oil at 150°C for 5 minutes, then drain and cool for 15 minutes.
Cook the onions in the butter over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden.
Mix the mayonnaise, tomato sauce and relish for the spread.
Roll the mince into 8 balls. Smash each one thin on a very hot griddle, season and brush the top with mustard. Cook 2 minutes, flip mustard side down, add a slice of cheese and cook 1 minute more.
Fry the fries again at 190°C for 3 minutes until crisp and toss with the salt.
Toast the buns cut side down. Build each with spread, lettuce, tomato, a patty, onions, pickles, a second patty and more spread. Serve with the fries.

The Big Lebowski (1998).n: Shomer shabbos coffee brisket on challah
The Big Lebowski (1998).note: Brisket braised low with onions, paprika and black Folgers coffee, piled on challah with horseradish cream and pickles. Cooked on Friday so Walter is done by sundown. He does not roll on Shabbos.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Rub the brisket with the paprika, salt and pepper.
Brown the brisket well in the oil in a heavy casserole, about 4 minutes a side, then lift it out.
Cook the onions in the same pot for 10 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and tomato paste and cook 1 minute more.
Stir in the brown sugar, coffee and stock, return the brisket, cover and braise in the oven for 3 and a half hours until it pulls apart.
Rest the brisket in its juices for 15 minutes, then slice it across the grain.
Slice the challah thickly. Pile on the brisket with a spoon of the onions and juices, the horseradish cream and pickles.

The Big Lebowski (1998).note: A puffed oven pancake with lingonberry jam, whipped crème fraîche, lemon and icing sugar. What the nihilists order at the coffee shop. They believe in nothing, except pancakes.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) with a 26cm cast-iron or ovenproof frying pan inside.
Blend the eggs, milk, flour, caster sugar, salt and vanilla until smooth.
Add the butter to the hot pan, swirl until it foams, pour in the batter and bake for 18 to 20 minutes until puffed high and golden. Keep the oven door shut.
Whip the crème fraîche with the lemon zest until it just holds its shape.
Take it to the table straight away. Spoon over the lingonberry jam and crème fraîche, squeeze over a little lemon juice and dust with the icing sugar.

The Big Lebowski (1998).note: Big choc chip cookies with dark chocolate and sea salt flakes, packed warm in a zip-lock bag. Found under the car seat. “Is this your homework, Larry?”
steps: Melt the butter in a small pan and cook for 4 minutes until it smells nutty and turns golden brown, then cool for 10 minutes.
Beat the brown butter with both sugars, the egg and vanilla until smooth.
Mix in the flour, bicarb soda, salt and chocolate.
Chill the dough for 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Roll 16 balls, space them on 2 lined trays and bake for 11 to 12 minutes until golden at the edges and soft in the middle.
Sprinkle with the sea salt flakes, cool on the trays for 10 minutes and pack in a zip-lock bag for the couch.

The Big Lebowski (1998).note: Vodka and coffee liqueur over ice, topped with half-and-half and stirred lazily. The Dude calls it a Caucasian. “Careful, man, there's a beverage here!”
steps: Fill four rocks glasses with the ice and pour 45ml vodka and 20ml coffee liqueur into each.
Stir the cream and milk together for a half-and-half, float 30ml on each drink and stir lazily.

The Big Lebowski (1998).note: Ice-cold sarsaparilla poured over vanilla ice cream, with a curl of lemon peel. The Stranger asks the barman for a good one.
steps: Chill four tall glasses in the freezer for 10 minutes.
Drop 2 scoops of ice cream into each glass.
Pour the sarsaparilla slowly down the side so it foams up without spilling over, and finish each with a curl of lemon peel.

The Departed (2006).note: Clams, potato and bacon in cream. Oyster crackers.
steps: Dice the bacon, onion, celery and potatoes.
Fry the bacon until crisp, then sweat the onion and celery in the fat until soft.
Add the potatoes, clam juice and thyme and simmer until the potato is tender.
Stir in the clam meat and cream and warm through. Serve in cups with oyster crackers.

The Departed (2006).note: Baked here each morning, cut thick, salted butter. Start at the bar.
steps: Mix the flours, bicarb and salt, then stir in the buttermilk to a soft dough. Shape into a round and cut a deep cross on top.
Bake at 220°C until golden and it sounds hollow when tapped underneath.
