Rest the loaf, then slice thick and serve with the salted butter.

The Departed (2006).note: White fish in lager batter, chips, minted mushy peas, malt vinegar.
steps: Cut the potatoes into chips, rinse and dry well. Whisk the batter flour, cornflour and cold lager together.
Fry the chips in oil at 140°C until pale and soft, then drain.
Cook the peas, then crush with the butter and chopped mint and keep warm.
Dust the fish in flour, dip in batter and fry at 180°C in batches until golden and crisp.
Fry the chips again at 185°C until crisp. Salt well and serve with the fish, peas and malt vinegar.

The Departed (2006).note: Sponge, vanilla custard, dark chocolate ganache.
steps: Whisk 4 of the eggs with half the sugar until thick and pale. Fold in the flour and divide between two lined 20cm tins.
Bake at 180°C until springy, then turn out and cool completely.
Heat the milk. Whisk 3 yolks with the remaining sugar and cornflour, whisk in the hot milk, return to the pan and stir until thick.
Chill the custard until cold and set.
Sandwich the sponges with custard. Melt the chocolate with the cream and pour over the top.
Juice the limes and orange.
Shake the cranberry juice, lime juice, orange juice and syrup with ice, then strain into 4 short glasses of crushed ice. Top with soda and a lime wedge. Add vodka first for the grown-up version.

The French Connection (1971).note: Chicken livers seared pink and flamed with cognac, blended with butter, shallot and thyme. Cornichons, warm baguette.
steps: Soften the shallot in a little butter, then sear the livers until just pink.
Add the cognac and flame it off carefully.
Blitz the livers, shallot and thyme with soft butter until smooth, then pack into a dish.
Pour melted butter over the top and chill until set.
Serve with cornichons and warm baguette.

The French Connection (1971).note: Drip coffee in a paper cup, two warm cake doughnuts rolled in cinnamon sugar.
steps: Warm the doughnuts in a 160°C oven.
Toss in the sugar mixed with the cinnamon.
Brew the coffee with the water and pour into paper cups.

The French Connection (1971).note: Sirloin seared hard and rested, warm tarragon and shallot butter sauce, hand-cut potatoes fried twice.
steps: Reduce the vinegar with tarragon and shallot until almost dry. Cut the potatoes into chips and dry them.
Fry the chips in the oil at 140°C, then drain.
Whisk the yolks with the reduction over low heat until thick, then drizzle in the warm butter to make the sauce.
Season the steaks with salt and pepper, sear hard, then rest.
Fry the chips again until crisp and serve with the steaks and sauce.

The French Connection (1971).note: Vanilla custard baked in a water bath, chilled, turned out under amber syrup.
steps: Melt part of the sugar to an amber caramel and pour into 4 ramekins.
Whisk the eggs and yolks with the remaining sugar, milk and the seeds of the vanilla bean, then pour over the caramel.
Bake in a water bath at 150°C until just set.
Chill overnight, then run a knife around the edge and turn out.

The French Connection (1971).note: Pastis and orgeat over ice, clouded with water.
steps: Put pastis and orgeat in each of 4 tall glasses, add ice, then pour in chilled water slowly and watch it cloud. Stir once and serve a jug of cold water on the side.

The Freshman (1990).note: Salami, mortadella, provolone, red peppers, artichokes.
ing: 2 roasted red capsicums, cut in strips
steps: Arrange the salami, mortadella and provolone on a board.
Add the capsicum strips and artichokes.
Tear the loaf at the table.

The Freshman (1990).note: Squid rings in a semolina crust, lemon and marinara.
steps: Slice the squid into rings and soak in the milk for 20 minutes.
Toss in the flour mixed with semolina and salt.
Fry in the oil at 190°C for 1 minute a batch.
Warm the marinara and serve with lemon.

The Freshman (1990).note: Butter-seared scaloppine, mushrooms, marsala pan sauce.
steps: Dust the veal in seasoned flour and sear in butter and oil for 1 minute a side, then set aside.
Brown the mushrooms, add the marsala and stock and reduce by half.
Whisk in the cold butter, return the veal and warm through.

The Freshman (1990).note: Vanilla ricotta, mini chocolate chips, pistachio ends. No animals were served. Allegedly.
steps: Drain the ricotta for 2 hours.
Beat with icing sugar and vanilla, then fold in the chocolate chips.
Pipe into the shells just before serving and dip the ends in pistachios.

The Freshman (1990).note: Bitter amaro, prosecco and soda on ice, orange wheel.
steps: Fill four large wine glasses with ice.
Add amaro to each, then prosecco and soda, and stir once gently.
Slide a thin orange wheel into each glass and serve straight away.

The Godfather (1972).note: Salami, aged provolone, olives and roasted peppers, at room temperature.
steps: Arrange the salami, provolone and olives on a platter.
Pile the roast capsicum alongside, drizzle with olive oil and add cracked pepper.
Leave out for a few minutes so it comes to room temperature before serving.

The Godfather (1972).note: Crisp risotto balls, fried golden round a melting mozzarella heart.
steps: Make the risotto the day before: soften 160g arborio in the butter, add 500ml hot stock a ladle at a time over about 20 minutes, stir in the parmesan, then spread it on a tray and chill overnight.
Cut the mozzarella into 8 cubes. Divide the cold risotto into 8 portions and wrap each around a cube, rolling into balls.
Roll the balls in flour, dip in the beaten egg and coat in breadcrumbs.
Chill the crumbed balls for 20 minutes so they hold their shape.
Heat the oil to 170°C and fry in batches until golden and hot through, about 4 to 5 minutes. Drain and finish with the sea salt.

The Godfather (1972).note: Pork and beef meatballs, fennel sausage, slow tomato, pecorino.
steps: Mix the mince with the egg, breadcrumbs, a share of the pecorino and a pinch of salt. Form 12 meatballs.
Brown the meatballs in olive oil with the sausages cut into chunks, then set aside.
Soften the onion in the same pot, add the garlic and tomato paste, then stir in the tomatoes and water.
Return the meat, cover partly and simmer gently, stirring and adding water if needed. Check the meatballs are cooked through.
Boil the rigatoni, toss with the sauce and serve with the meat and the rest of the pecorino.

The Godfather (1972).note: Crisp shells, orange-scented ricotta, dark chocolate, crushed pistachio.
ing: 40g icing sugar, plus extra for dusting
steps: Drain the ricotta in a lined sieve in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
Beat the ricotta with the icing sugar and orange zest, then fold in the chocolate.
Pipe into the cannoli shells just before serving.
Dip the ends in crushed pistachios and dust lightly with icing sugar.

The Godfather (1972).note: Ruby citrus syrup, cold seltzer. An orange on every table.
steps: Fill 4 glasses with ice.
Add the syrup to each glass and top with sparkling water. Stir gently, adjusting syrup to taste.
Finish each with a thin twist of orange.

The Godfather Part II (1974).note: Saffron rice, beef ragù, peas and a mozzarella heart.
steps: Cook the rice in the stock with the saffron, stirring, until thick. Stir in the parmesan, spread on a tray and chill, ideally overnight.
Brown the mince with the peas and passata until thick and dry. Cool.
Wrap golf-ball portions of cold rice around a spoon of filling and a cube of mozzarella.
Roll in flour, egg and breadcrumbs.
Fry in the oil at 175°C in batches until deep gold and hot through, then drain.

The Godfather Part II (1974).note: Ham, roast pork, Swiss, pickle, mustard, pressed hot.
steps: Split the rolls and smear the cut sides with mustard.
Layer with ham, pork, Swiss cheese and pickle.
Brush the tops with melted butter.
Press in a heavy pan over medium heat with a second pan on top, about 3 minutes a side, until the cheese melts.

The Godfather Part II (1974).note: Eggplant and slow tomato, ricotta, blistered mozzarella.
steps: Fry the eggplant in the oil until soft and browned, add the garlic for a minute, then the passata and half the basil, torn. Simmer slowly until thick.
Cook the ziti or penne 3 minutes short of done and drain.
Mix the ricotta with the parmesan, nutmeg and the rest of the basil, chopped.
Layer pasta, sauce and ricotta in a baking dish and top with mozzarella.
Bake at 200°C until blistered.

The Godfather Part II (1974).note: Vanilla slab cake iced pale green, shaped like the island.
ing: green food colouring, a few drops
steps: Beat the butter and caster sugar, add the eggs, then fold in the flour and milk.
Bake in a lined slab tin at 180°C.
Cool completely, then trim into a rough island shape.
Beat the icing butter with icing sugar and colouring. Spread thinly, then again, and pipe happy birthday across.
Dissolve the sugar in the hot water and cool to make syrup.
Chill four coupes.
For each drink, shake rum, lime juice and syrup hard with plenty of ice, then double strain into a coupe.

The Godfather Part III (1990).note: Chickpea fritters with parsley, fried crisp. Salt and a squeeze of lemon.
steps: Whisk the chickpea flour into the cold water with the salt until smooth.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until very thick.
Stir in the parsley and spread 1cm thick on an oiled tray. Leave to set for 1 hour.
Cut into squares and fry in 180°C oil in batches until puffed and golden.
Drain, season with the flaky salt and serve with lemon wedges.

The Godfather Part III (1990).note: Ripe cantaloupe, cured ham, cracked pepper and olive oil.
steps: Leave the rockmelon at room temperature for an hour.
Halve, deseed, cut into 12 long wedges and cut off the skin.
Drape each wedge with prosciutto, add pepper and a drizzle of olive oil just before serving.

The Godfather Part III (1990).note: Rigatoni, fried eggplant, tomato and basil, under grated ricotta salata.
steps: Cut the eggplants into thick half moons and fry in batches in most of the olive oil until deep gold. Drain.
Fry the garlic in 2 tbsp of oil, add the tomatoes and basil, simmer and season.
Cook the rigatoni until al dente.
Toss the pasta with the sauce, eggplant and a splash of pasta water. Grate ricotta salata heavily over the top.

The Godfather Part III (1990).note: Crisp shells filled to order with sweet ricotta, candied orange, pistachio.
ing: 80g icing sugar, plus extra for dusting
steps: Drain the ricotta in a sieve for 2 hours.
Beat with icing sugar, cinnamon and candied peel.
Pipe into the shells just before serving.
Dip each end in pistachios and dust with icing sugar.

The Godfather Part III (1990).note: Lemon liqueur on ice, prosecco and soda, lemon peel and mint.
steps: Fill four large wine glasses with ice.
Pour limoncello into each, top with prosecco and soda and stir once gently.
Peel a wide strip of lemon zest per glass, twist over the drink and drop in. Finish with mint.

The Out-of-Towners (1970).note: Butter shortbread sandwiched with raspberry jam, dusted with sugar. Safer than Cracker Jacks.
ing: 120g icing sugar, plus extra to dust
steps: Beat the butter and icing sugar until pale. Mix in the flour and cornflour to a soft dough.
Press into a lined 20 x 30cm tin and prick all over.
Bake at 160°C until pale golden.
Cut into 24 fingers while warm and cool in the tin.
Sandwich pairs with jam and dust with icing sugar.

The Out-of-Towners (1970).note: Glazed sticky with honey, mustard, brown sugar and Worcestershire, on picks with pearl onions.
steps: Simmer the franks in water, then drain.
Melt the butter with the honey, Dijon, sugar and Worcestershire in a frying pan.
Add the franks and toss over medium heat until sticky and glazed.
Serve on toothpicks with cocktail onions.

The Out-of-Towners (1970).note: Seared to order and rested, two eggs fried, hash browns and buttered toast.
ing: 800g rib eye steak, in four pieces
steps: Grate the potatoes and squeeze dry in a tea towel. Season and shape into 4 hash browns.
Fry the hash browns in some of the butter over medium heat, turning once.
Sear the steaks in a very hot pan with the oil to about 54°C, then rest.
Fry the eggs in butter.
Toast the sourdough and butter it. Serve a steak, two eggs, a hash brown and a toast each.

The Out-of-Towners (1970).note: Baked slowly in a water bath on a crumb crust, chilled overnight, crowned with sliced strawberries.
steps: Crush the biscuits, mix with the butter and press into a lined 18cm springform tin.
Beat the cream cheese and sugar, then mix in the sour cream, eggs and vanilla. Pour over the base.
Wrap the tin in two layers of foil and stand in a roasting dish with hot water halfway up its sides.
Bake at 150°C until the centre gently wobbles.
Cool, then refrigerate overnight.
Top with strawberries and cut into portions.

The Out-of-Towners (1970).note: Gin and dry vermouth stirred very cold, strained, one green olive.
steps: Freeze the martini glasses.
Stir the gin and vermouth over ice in batches, then strain into the glasses.
Garnish each with an olive.

The Pope of Greenwich Village (1984).note: On the half shell under garlic, oregano and parmesan crumbs.
steps: Steam the clams with a splash of water in a covered pan until they open, about 4 minutes. Discard any that stay closed.
Remove the top shells.
Mix the breadcrumbs, garlic, oregano, parmesan and olive oil and top each clam.
Grill for 3 minutes until golden.

The Pope of Greenwich Village (1984).note: Ripe cantaloupe, sliced ham, bocconcini in basil oil.
steps: Cut the rockmelon into 12 skinless wedges and drape with prosciutto.
Blitz the basil with olive oil and salt.
Drain the bocconcini, dress with the basil oil and pepper, and serve beside the melon.

The Pope of Greenwich Village (1984).note: Escalopes seared in butter, button mushrooms, glossy wine sauce.
steps: Dust the veal in the seasoned flour and sear in butter and oil for 1 minute a side, then set aside.
Brown the mushrooms in the same pan, add the marsala and stock and reduce by half.
Whisk in the cold butter, return the veal and warm through for a minute.
Serve with crusty bread.

The Pope of Greenwich Village (1984).note: Marsala custard whisked warm at your table, over strawberries.
steps: Whisk the yolks, sugar and marsala in a heatproof bowl over simmering water for 6 to 8 minutes until thick, pale and tripled in volume.
Halve the strawberries into four glasses.
Spoon the warm zabaglione over and serve straight away.

The Pope of Greenwich Village (1984).note: Red aperitivo, sweet vermouth, soda and orange. Paulie's tab.
steps: Fill four tumblers with ice.
Pour aperitivo and vermouth into each glass and stir for 10 seconds.
Top with soda, stir once and tuck a half-moon of orange into each glass.
Butter the bread.
Layer the ham, cheddar and pickles across four slices and top with the other slices.
Trim off the crusts and cut each sandwich into three fingers.
Wrap in baking paper and refrigerate until serving.

The Secret of My Success (1987).note: Kernels and spring onions in egg batter, fried crisp. Sour cream.
steps: Cut the kernels from the cobs.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, egg and milk into a thick batter. Stir in the corn, spring onions and salt.
Shallow-fry spoonfuls of batter in the neutral oil in batches over medium heat, turning once, until golden and cooked through.
Drain and serve with sour cream for dipping.

The Secret of My Success (1987).note: Iron pan, butter, garlic and thyme.
ing: 800g rib eye steak, in four pieces
steps: Pat the steaks dry, salt them evenly and refrigerate uncovered to dry-brine, at least 4 hours.
Heat a heavy pan over high heat with the oil.
Sear the steaks in batches, turning once.
Lower the heat, add the butter, thyme and garlic and baste repeatedly.
Rest the steaks, then slice and spoon over the pan butter.
Line a 20cm pie dish with half the pastry.
Peel, core and slice the apples and toss with sugar and cinnamon.
Fill the crust, cover with the remaining pastry, crimp, cut steam vents, brush with egg and sprinkle with a little sugar.
Bake at 190°C until golden and tender.
Rest, then divide into four portions and serve with ice cream.
Freeze four martini glasses.
Working in two batches, stir the gin and vermouth with ice.
Strain equally into the frozen glasses.
Express the lemon twist oils over each drink and garnish.

The Taking of Pelham One Two Three (1974.note: Puff pastry corners folded over a sweet, lemony filling, then iced.
steps: Beat the cream cheese with the sugar, egg yolk and lemon zest. Cut the pastry into 8 squares.
Spoon the filling into the middle of each square and fold in the corners.
Bake at 200°C until golden.
Cool, then drizzle with the icing sugar mixed with lemon juice.

The Taking of Pelham One Two Three (1974.note: Jam filled, rolled in sugar while still warm.
steps: Warm the doughnuts on a tray at 160°C.
Roll each straight away in the sugar so it sticks and serve on a plate in the middle of the table.

The Taking of Pelham One Two Three (1974.note: Sliced breast, shredded iceberg, tomato and mayonnaise on a long roll, wrapped tight.
steps: Split the rolls and spread with mayonnaise.
Layer with turkey, Swiss cheese, lettuce and tomato. Season.
Close, wrap tightly in paper and cut in half.

The Taking of Pelham One Two Three (1974.note: Cream cheese dough, apricot jam, walnuts and cinnamon sugar.
steps: Rub the butter and cream cheese into the flour to form a dough.
Chill the dough.
Roll into circles, spread with jam, walnuts and cinnamon sugar, cut into wedges and roll up from the wide end.
Bake at 180°C until golden.

The Taking of Pelham One Two Three (1974.note: Whisky, honey, lemon and fresh ginger, topped with boiling water. Cinnamon stick.
steps: Thinly slice the ginger and juice the lemons, keeping a few wheels.
Into each of 4 heatproof glasses put whisky, honey, lemon juice and ginger slices, top with boiling water and stir until the honey dissolves. Add a lemon wheel and a cinnamon stick.

The Untouchables (1987).note: Fried in the hotel kitchen, tomato sauce on the side.
steps: Cook the rice in the stock to a firm risotto, stir in the parmesan and cool completely.
Roll into 16 balls around cubes of mozzarella.
Roll in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs.
Heat the neutral oil to 180°C and fry for 4 minutes in batches.
Warm the passata and serve for dipping.

The Untouchables (1987).note: Laid down the middle of the round table, before the bat comes out.
ing: 1 jar roast peppers, torn into strips
steps: Fold the salami, mortadella and prosciutto onto a long board.
Add the artichokes and peppers, and dress the bocconcini with olive oil, salt and pepper.
Slice the loaf and serve alongside so everyone builds their own.

The Untouchables (1987).note: Shaved thin, dipped in the jus, hot peppers on top.
ing: 2 tsp dried oregano, plus 1 tsp for the jus
1 tsp black pepper, plus more for the jus
steps: Rub the beef with salt, pepper and oregano and roast at 200°C to 52°C inside.
Chill the beef well, then shave it thin.
Simmer the stock with the garlic, oregano and plenty of pepper.
Warm the beef in the jus, pile into the rolls, dip the whole sandwich and top with giardiniera.

The Untouchables (1987).note: From the Italian bakers on Taylor Street.
steps: Mix the ricotta, eggs, sugar, vanilla and lemon zest, then fold in the flour.
Drop teaspoons into 175°C oil and fry in batches for 3 minutes until puffed and golden.
Drain and toss in icing sugar.

The Untouchables (1987).note: Capone's own beer. Every bar in town has to stock it.
steps: Chill the bottles of lager in the fridge for at least 3 hours, then keep them cold in a tub of ice.
Pour the lager into heavy glass steins straight down the middle so each gets a proper head.

The Untouchables (1987).note: Down from the border by the truckload.
steps: Put one large ice cube in each of 4 short glasses.
Pour 30ml Canadian rye whisky over the ice in each glass.
Add a small splash of cold water to each to open up the whisky and serve.

The Untouchables (1987).note: Bourbon and bitters, the night Ness finally drinks. Here endeth the lesson.
steps: Dissolve the sugar in the hot water to make syrup.
For each drink, stir rye, syrup and bitters over ice for 30 seconds and strain over a large cube.
Twist a strip of orange peel over the top.

The Warriors (1979).note: Brushed with butter, served warm. Sharp cheddar dip, yellow mustard.
steps: Mix the flour (keeping a spoonful back for the cheese dip), yeast, sugar, salt and warm water, then knead until smooth.
Cover and rise until doubled.
Roll into ropes and cut into 24 bites. Bring the boiling water and bicarbonate of soda to a simmer.
Boil the bites in batches for 20 seconds, then drain on baking paper.
Bake at 220°C until deep golden, then brush with melted butter and coarse salt.
For the dip, melt butter, stir in the remaining flour, whisk in the milk and simmer. Off the heat, stir in the cheddar and serve with mustard.

The Warriors (1979).note: Charred ribs off the cob, chilli butter, lime, smoked salt.
steps: Quarter the cobs lengthways on a secure board with a sturdy sharp knife (use whole cobs if easier). Melt the butter with the chilli flakes and smoked salt.
Brush the corn with the chilli butter.
Roast at 220°C, turning once, until tender and charred at the edges. Finish with lime juice.

The Warriors (1979).note: Griddled beef franks, beef chilli, onion, mustard. Shoestring fries.
steps: Dice the onion and keep a quarter aside for topping. Mince the garlic.
Fry the rest of the onion in the oil with the garlic, then add the mince and brown well.
Stir in the tomato paste, cumin, smoked paprika, tomatoes and water and simmer. Season with salt.
Bake the fries as directed on the packet.
Griddle the franks until piping hot and warm the buns. Fill with franks and chilli and finish with onion and mustard.

The Warriors (1979).note: Vanilla between chewy chocolate cookies, dipped in dark chocolate.
steps: Soften the ice cream just enough to scoop and sandwich between the cookies to make 4 sandwiches.
Freeze on a lined tray until firm.
Melt the chocolate gently and cool until just warm. Dip half of each sandwich.
Return to the freezer to set.

The Warriors (1979).note: Ice-cold cola, cherry syrup, a squeeze of lime.
steps: Fill 4 glasses with ice, add cherry syrup to each, top with cola and squeeze in a lime wedge. Stir once and taste before adding more syrup.

There's Something About Mary (1998).note: Crumbed risotto balls, mozzarella middle, marinara. Arancini. Have you seen my baseball?
steps: Soften the onion in the butter, stir in the rice, then add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, until creamy and just tender.
Stir in the parmesan, season, spread on a tray and chill until firm.
Roll into 12 balls, pushing a cube of mozzarella into the middle of each.
Roll in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
Simmer the passata with the garlic and a few basil leaves while the oil heats.
Fry the arancini at 180°C in batches until deep golden, drain and serve with the marinara and torn basil.

There's Something About Mary (1998).note: Garlic butter knots, parmesan, marinara. Healy spies on Mary in Miami.
steps: Cut the dough into 12 strips, roll each into a rope and tie in a loose knot.
Prove on a lined tray for 10 minutes, then bake at 220°C until golden.
Melt the butter with the garlic for a minute and stir in the parsley.
Toss the hot knots in the garlic butter and parmesan and serve with warm marinara.

There's Something About Mary (1998).note: Smoky franks, molasses baked beans, slaw. Franks and beans, Ted's prom night disaster.
ing: 2 x 400g tins of cannellini beans, drained
steps: Fry the bacon and onion in an ovenproof pot until soft and golden.
Stir in the beans, tomatoes, molasses, sugar, mustard, vinegar and water and bring to a simmer.
Bake uncovered at 170°C, stirring once, until thick and dark.
Toss the slaw with the mayo, and grill the franks until blistered.
Serve the franks on the beans with slaw alongside.

There's Something About Mary (1998).note: Ham and swiss chicken, crumbed, mustard cream. Puffy ends up in a full body cast.
steps: Cut a deep pocket into each breast and fill with a folded slice of ham and cheese.
Dust in flour, dip in egg and press into the panko.
Brown in the oil on both sides, then bake at 200°C until cooked through.
Warm the cream with the mustard and season, and steam the beans.
Slice the chicken and serve with the beans and the mustard cream.

There's Something About Mary (1998).n: Hair gel meringues with lemon curd
There's Something About Mary (1998).note: Vanilla meringues, whipped cream, lemon curd. Meringues. Mary thinks it's hair gel.
steps: Whisk the whites to soft peaks, then add the sugar a spoon at a time until thick and glossy.
Whisk in the vinegar, cornflour and vanilla and spoon 8 swirled mounds onto lined trays.
Bake at 120°C until crisp outside, then turn the oven off and let them cool inside.
Whip the cream with a little vanilla, and top each meringue with cream, lemon curd and blueberries.

There's Something About Mary (1998).note: Pineapple, ginger beer, rum and lime sorbet. Pineapple punch for the senior prom.
steps: Stir the rum, pineapple and lime juice in a punch bowl with ice.
Top with the ginger beer.
Float the sorbet on top and ladle into cups.

Things to Do in Denver When You're Dead.note: Six halves, yolks whipped with Dijon and pickle juice, smoked paprika, chives.
steps: Boil the eggs hard in a pot of simmering water.
Cool the eggs in iced water, then peel and halve them.
Mash the yolks with the mayonnaise, Dijon, pickle juice, salt and pepper until smooth.
Pipe or spoon the yolk mix back into the whites. Finish with smoked paprika and chopped chives.

Things to Do in Denver When You're Dead.note: Melted white cheese, roasted green chiles, garlic, cumin. Corn chips to dunk.
steps: Crush the garlic and drain the green chiles.
Melt the cheese with the milk over low heat, stirring until smooth.
Stir in the chiles, garlic and cumin and simmer, then pour into a warm bowl. Serve straight away with the corn chips.

Things to Do in Denver When You're Dead.note: Thin beef patty, Swiss and slow onions on rye, griddled crisp in butter.
steps: Cook the onions in a little of the butter over low heat until soft and golden.
Shape the mince into 4 thin oval patties, season, and sear in a hot pan until browned on both sides.
Butter the bread on the outside. Build each sandwich with a patty, onions and two slices of Swiss cheese.
Griddle the sandwiches in a pan over medium heat, turning once, until crisp and the cheese has melted.

Things to Do in Denver When You're Dead.note: Puffed fried pastry pillows, warm honey, a dust of cinnamon.
steps: Mix the flour, baking powder and salt. Rub in the butter, then add the warm water and mix to a soft dough.
Rest the dough, covered, so it relaxes.
Roll the dough out 3mm thick and cut into 16 squares.
Fry in batches in oil heated to 180°C for about a minute a side, until puffed and golden. Drain on paper towel.
Drizzle with honey and dust with cinnamon.

Things to Do in Denver When You're Dead.note: Rum, pineapple, coconut cream, blended. Umbrella.
steps: Toast the coconut in a dry pan until golden, then cool on a plate.
Wet the rims of 4 glasses with a lime wedge and dip in the toasted coconut. Juice the limes and cut the pineapple into wedges.
Blend the rum, pineapple juice, coconut cream, lime juice and ice until thick and smooth.
Pour into the glasses and finish with a pineapple wedge and a cocktail umbrella.

Three Men and a Baby (1987).note: Ginger and spring onion on white bread, sesame, fried. Chilli dip.
steps: Blitz the prawns with the egg white, ginger, spring onion and salt.
Spread on the bread and press in the sesame seeds.
Cut into triangles.
Fry in oil at 180°C until golden, then drain.
Serve with sweet chilli sauce.

Three Men and a Baby (1987).note: Day-old bagels, baked crisp. Chive and lemon cream cheese.
steps: Slice the bagels into thin rounds and brush with oil.
Bake at 180°C until crisp.
Beat the cream cheese with chives and lemon zest.
Serve the chips around the schmear.

Three Men and a Baby (1987).note: Seared sirloin, butter onions, horseradish mayo and Swiss on sourdough.
steps: Cook the onions in butter over low heat until soft and golden.
Sear the steak hard, turning once, then rest and slice thin.
Mix the mayonnaise with the horseradish.
Toast the sourdough, spread with mayo, pile on steak and onions, top with Swiss and grill until melted.

Three Men and a Baby (1987).note: Yolks, sugar and hot milk, stirred thick. Warm or cold.
steps: Heat the milk with the vanilla bean until steaming.
Whisk the yolks, sugar and cornflour in a bowl.
Pour on the hot milk, then return to the pan and stir over low heat until thick.
Serve warm, or chill with plastic pressed on the surface.

Three Men and a Baby (1987).note: Whole milk, vanilla, honey, shaken on ice. Nutmeg.
steps: Shake the bourbon, milk, syrup and vanilla with ice until frothy.
Strain into 4 ice-filled glasses.
Grate nutmeg over the top.

Tootsie (1982).note: Egg salad with watercress, and cucumber with cream cheese, on soft white bread. Crusts off, cut in triangles.
steps: Boil the eggs, then cool.
Mash the eggs with mayonnaise and cress.
Spread cream cheese on some of the bread and layer with cucumber.
Make up the sandwiches, cut off the crusts and cut into triangles.

Tootsie (1982).note: Charred under the grill, peeled, whipped smooth with feta, yoghurt, garlic, hot chilli flakes and olive oil. Sesame crackers.
ing: 2 tbsp olive oil, plus extra to drizzle
steps: Char the capsicums under a hot grill.
Cover, then peel and seed.
Blitz with the feta, yoghurt, garlic, chilli and oil until smooth.
Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with oil and serve with crackers.

Tootsie (1982).note: Butter, grated lemon peel and thyme under the skin. Carved, with potatoes browned in the drippings.
steps: Salt the chicken and refrigerate uncovered overnight to dry-brine.
Mix the butter with lemon zest and thyme and push under the skin.
Roast at 220°C with the potatoes in the tray.
Lower to 180°C and roast until cooked through.
Rest before carving.

Tootsie (1982).note: Cream biscuits baked this morning, split and filled with sugared berries and soft whipped cream.
steps: Mix the flour, 200ml of the cream and some of the sugar to a soft dough.
Pat out, cut 4 rounds and bake at 220°C.
Toss the strawberries with sugar.
Whip the remaining cream softly.
Split the scones and fill with berries and cream.

Tootsie (1982).note: Strong and black, poured into glasses. Lemon and cherry preserves on the side, to stir in.
steps: Brew the tea in the just-boiled water and strain into 4 glasses.
Serve with lemon slices and a small dish of cherry jam on the side for stirring in.

Trading Places (1983).note: Prunes stuffed with a whole almond, rolled in Lancaster bacon and baked crisp.
steps: Push an almond into each prune.
Wrap each in half a rasher of bacon and secure with a toothpick.
Bake at 200°C until the bacon is crisp.
Serve warm.

Trading Places (1983).note: Cos, coddled egg, anchovy and Parmesan, dressed at your table.
steps: Tear the sourdough into small pieces and fry in the butter, tossing, until golden and crisp. Drain.
Lower the egg into simmering water for 1 minute, then cool it under the tap.
Mash the garlic and anchovies to a paste in a big bowl. Crack in the coddled egg, add the lemon juice, Worcestershire and mustard, then whisk in the oil slowly until thick.
Add the cos leaves, whole or torn, and toss at the table until every leaf is coated.
Shave the parmesan over, scatter the croutons and serve straight away.

Trading Places (1983).note: Standing rib, salted a day ahead, roasted slow and carved to order. Natural juices, horseradish cream, browned potatoes. Ask for the end cut early.
steps: Salt the roast the day before and leave it uncovered in the fridge.
Roast at 120°C until 52°C inside.
Rest the beef.
Roast the potatoes in oil at 200°C while the beef rests.
Blast the beef at 260°C for a crust.
Simmer the pan juices with the stock for jus.
Carve and serve with horseradish cream, potatoes and jus.

Trading Places (1983).note: Grated rind and juice in the batter, brushed warm with thick orange syrup.
steps: Beat the butter, most of the sugar and the orange zest until pale.
Add the eggs, then fold in the flour with the orange juice.
Bake in a lined tin at 170°C.
Boil the concentrate with the remaining sugar and brush over the warm cake.

Trading Places (1983).note: Fresh-squeezed juice and chilled champagne, half and half.
steps: Squeeze the oranges and chill the juice well.
Fill four flutes halfway with juice and gently top with sparkling wine, pouring slowly.

Wall-E (2008).note: Hollowed loaf filled with ham, roast pepper, pesto, mozzarella and spinach, pressed and sliced. Packed tight, like the cooler he carries his finds home in.
steps: Cut the top off the loaf and pull out most of the soft inside.
Spread the pesto inside the loaf.
Layer in the ham, capsicum, mozzarella, spinach, salami and tomatoes, pressing each layer down.
Put the lid back on, wrap tightly in cling wrap and press under a heavy pot in the fridge overnight.
Cut into wedges to serve.

Wall-E (2008).note: Peas crushed with mint, feta, lemon and olive oil, green shoots on top, crunchy pita chips. He found the seedling in an old fridge and kept it in a boot.
steps: Cook 400g frozen peas for 3 minutes, drain and cool under cold water.
Pulse with a handful of mint, 100g feta, the zest and juice of a lemon, 3 tbsp olive oil and salt until roughly smashed.
Cut 4 pita breads into triangles, brush with oil and bake at 190°C for 10 minutes until crisp.
Pile the smash into a bowl, stand a few pea shoots in the middle and serve with the chips.

Wall-E (2008).note: Marshmallow puffed rice, cut into cubes and stacked into towers. Compacted and stacked, like his towers over the city.
steps: Line a square tray with baking paper.
Melt the butter and marshmallows together over low heat.
Stir through the puffed rice until well coated.
Press firmly into the tray and leave to set.
Cut into neat cubes and stack into towers.

Wall-E (2008).n: Pumpkin lentil soup in a mug
Wall-E (2008).note: Pumpkin, red lentil and coconut soup with ginger, in big mugs with a straw. Sipped through a straw, the way everyone on the Axiom eats.
steps: Soften the onion and ginger in the oil.
Add the pumpkin, lentils, coconut milk and water and simmer until everything is soft.
Blitz the soup until smooth.
Make grilled cheese from the sourdough, cheddar and butter.
Serve the soup in big mugs with a straw and the toasties on the side.

Wall-E (2008).n: Earth garden veg and haloumi tray
Wall-E (2008).note: Pumpkin, capsicum, zucchini and chickpeas roasted with honey and cumin, golden haloumi, mint and lemon yoghurt. The captain learns food comes out of the ground.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C.
Toss 600g pumpkin chunks, 2 capsicums, 2 red onions in wedges, 2 zucchini and 1 drained tin chickpeas with 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tbsp honey and salt.
Roast for 35 minutes, turning once.
Slice 250g haloumi and fry until golden.
Mix 200g Greek yoghurt with lemon juice and salt.
Top the tray with haloumi, drizzle with yoghurt and scatter with mint.

Wall-E (2008).note: Light sponge fingers split and filled with piped vanilla cream. Cream-filled snack cakes, the one thing tougher than his cockroach.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a tray.
Whisk the eggs and sugar until pale and thick, then fold in the flour.
Pipe 12 fingers onto the tray and bake.
Cool, then whip the cream with the vanilla.
Split the sponges and pipe in the cream.

Wall-E (2008).note: Frozen raspberries, lemon and blue cordial blended with ice. The chair screens switch the whole deck from red to blue.
steps: Blend the raspberries, lemon juice, cordial, sugar, water and ice until smooth and slushy.
Pour into tall cups, add a lemon wheel and a straw and serve straight away.

When Harry Met Sally... (1989).note: Half-sours in rye batter. Pickles come with every table.
steps: Cut the pickles into spears and pat them very dry. Keep a teaspoon of the brine.
Whisk the plain flour, rye flour, paprika and cold soda water into a thin batter.
Dip the spears and fry at 180°C for about 2 minutes until crisp, in batches. Drain on a rack and salt lightly.
Stir the mayonnaise with the mustard and the pickle brine and serve alongside.

When Harry Met Sally... (1989).note: Ham, turkey, swiss and egg. Dressing on the side.
steps: Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Wash the cos lettuces, dry well and tear into a large platter.
Arrange the leg ham, turkey, swiss cheese strips, halved eggs, tomatoes and cucumber in rows over the lettuce.
Pour the olive oil and red wine vinegar into two little jugs and serve them on the side.

When Harry Met Sally... (1989).note: The Katz's classic. Hand cut, piled high, a pickle on the side.
steps: Steam the pastrami over gently boiling water until glossy, soft and piping hot.
Spread the rye with mustard.
Pile the pastrami high on four slices and close the sandwiches.
Serve each with a pickle on the side.

When Harry Met Sally... (1989).note: Heated, with the ice cream on the side.
ing: 300ml strawberry ice cream, or 150ml thickened cream if unavailable
steps: Cut four slices from the pie.
Warm on a tray at 180°C.
Serve with the strawberry ice cream in a separate small bowl beside each slice.

When Harry Met Sally... (1989).note: Chocolate syrup, milk and soda. I'll have what she's having.
steps: Pour 30ml chocolate syrup into each of four tall glasses and add 100ml ice cold milk.
Blast the soda water in hard from a height until the foam reaches the rim, stirring fast with a long spoon as it goes. Serve straight away. No egg, no cream.

Working Girl (1988).note: Chilled, on cucumber rounds with Russian dressing and dill.
steps: Poach the prawns until just pink, chill and peel.
Cut the cucumbers into thick rounds.
Mix the mayonnaise and tomato sauce.
Top each round with a prawn, a dot of sauce and a dill sprig. Serve cold.

Working Girl (1988).note: A pair, bound with egg, mayonnaise, Dijon and crumbs, browned in butter. Lemon, tartar sauce.
steps: Mix the crab, mayonnaise, egg, Dijon, parsley and breadcrumbs.
Shape 12 small cakes and chill.
Pan-fry in butter, turning once, until golden.
Serve with lemon wedges and tartare sauce.

Working Girl (1988).note: Seared hard, carved thin over cos lettuce, cherry tomatoes, red onion and blue cheese. Red wine vinaigrette. Big ideas? Try the steak.
steps: Sear the steaks hard in a hot pan, then rest.
Toss the cos with the tomatoes and onion.
Whisk the vinegar, oil and Dijon.
Slice the steak thin and arrange over the salad with dressing and blue cheese.

Working Girl (1988).note: Butter sponge, raspberry jam, Swiss meringue buttercream.
steps: Beat the first batch of butter with half the sugar, add the whole eggs and fold in the flour.
Bake in two tins at 175°C.
Cool the cakes.
Whisk the whites with the rest of the sugar over hot water until thick and glossy.
Beat in the remaining butter, a little at a time, to make the buttercream.
Layer the cakes with jam and buttercream and chill.

Working Girl (1988).note: Bourbon stirred cold with sweet vermouth and bitters, served up with a cherry.
steps: Stir the bourbon, vermouth and bitters with ice.
Strain into 4 chilled coupes and drop a cherry in each.

You've Got Mail (1998).note: Two dozen cucumber rounds with dill cream cheese, capers and cracked pepper.
steps: Cut the cucumbers into 1.5cm rounds and pat dry.
Beat the cream cheese with the chopped dill and lemon zest.
Pipe or spoon onto each round.
Top with salmon, capers, a dill sprig and pepper.

You've Got Mail (1998).note: Three to an order, with spring onion cream cheese and cracked pepper.
steps: Halve the bagels and toast under a medium grill until golden.
Whip the cream cheese with the spring onions and pepper.
Spread over the eight halves and serve two halves per person.

You've Got Mail (1998).note: Cranberry sauce on buttered sourdough, pressed hot until the cheese runs.
steps: Spread the sourdough with cranberry sauce.
Divide the turkey and brie among four slices and close.
Butter the outsides.
Press in a hot sandwich pan or frying pan weighted with a second pan, turning once, until golden and the brie melts.
Cut each sandwich in half.

You've Got Mail (1998).note: Baked rich and dense, with sugared fresh strawberries.
steps: Crush the biscuits, mix with the butter and press into a lined tin.
Beat the cream cheese with the sugar, sour cream, eggs and vanilla.
Pour over the base and bake at 150°C until the centre gently wobbles.
Cool, then chill overnight.
Toss the strawberries with sugar and leave to macerate.
Cut four slices and serve with the strawberries and juices.

You've Got Mail (1998).note: Two shots of decaf espresso, steamed milk and a deep crown of foam.
steps: Grind the beans and brew four double espressos into warmed tall cups.
Steam the milk in batches, with enough air for a deep foam cap.
Divide the milk among the cups and spoon the foam on top.
